title: Adding a space to a select2 search term creates a request that returns > 150MB
body:
To reproduce (make sure you have the network tab visible first):
1. Go to a CHP Area
2. Click Edit
3. Click on the supervisor dropdown to bring up the search box
4. Type in the name of a branch, then wait until you see the `contacts_by_type_freetext` view request.
5. Type in a space.
6. You should see a second `contacts_by_type_freetext` view request with no key. If you keep waiting (about 4 minutes in production), it will download what appears to be every contact (about 190 MB in production), and the window might freeze.

Can we add in some sort of protection so that adding a space to the end of a search term can't start a whole new search (`contacts_by_type_freetext` request)? This may not fit in with how other searches work, but this can cause some annoying performance issues, including the web app freezing and search results taking a long time to be returned.

title: If initial sync fails without syncing anything subsequent syncs get no results
body:
If you only have the ddoc in your local db then the changes request is [incorrectly determined to be a app status watcher](https://github.com/medic/medic-api/blob/2.8.x/handlers/changes.js#L326) instead of a data replicator meaning it only watches for ddoc changes. This affects 2.8.0 and master.

The workaround is to clear your IDB and try again, but with some users the initial sync is likely to fail again, leaving them unable to use the app.

title: Initial sync fails if server doesn't respond within 30 seconds
body:
With some users initial replication isn't responding quickly enough and the request times out. This means the app loads with lots of errors. Eventually the background replication should fix the app and a refresh will get back to normal but it's a jarring experience. It should have a heartbeat so timeout doesn't occur unless the server is unreachable.

Affects 2.8.0

Causes #2770

title: Medic OS: cron.daily and related directories are broken and/or confusing
body:
Our OS images currently maintain two sets of `.d` directories for `cron` – one ephemeral directory beneath `/etc` intended to be used programmatically by packages, and one beneath `/srv/settings/system-services/cron` that is persistent. This is confusing.

Make `/srv/settings/system-services/cron/*.d` the sole set of user-accessible `.d` directories, and symlink the `/etc` versions to the real ones. If the packaging system needs its own ephemeral `cron.daily` directory, create a new one and bury it somewhere where an SSH session doesn't mistake it for human-accessible configuration.

Finally, ensure that all of the cron `.d` directories are present beneath `/etc`. On current instances in production, only `/etc/cron.daily` is present.

body:
Currently, the tasks titles include the patient name (things like `"{{contact.name}} referral follow up"`), because so far we've been displaying the task name on a single line so you need to stuff all the info in the name.

It's not working very well on small screens:
![screen shot 2016-09-29 at 14 54 50](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/911434/18962209/34692086-8670-11e6-9b4e-4a2baa387d7e.png)

The new People tab will have patient name split out to a separate line, which will help : 
![screen shot 2016-09-29 at 17 19 24 copy](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/911434/18962250/58d4c01a-8670-11e6-9ade-4382b091e52e.png)

But! With the current configs, with patient name included in the title, you get this, which defeats the purpose : 
![screen shot 2016-09-29 at 18 15 07](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/911434/18962327/b5afbb00-8670-11e6-9efc-20baa7b36431.png)
The name is duplicated, and the wrap is bad (screenshot is 320px)

So! I vote we edit the existing configs, to change task titles from e.g. `"{{contact.name}} referral follow up"` to  `"Referral follow up"`. We can roll it out along with the People tab update.
But since I'm not the one really in charge of updates, please give your opinions @garethbowen @sglangevin @abbyad (who is OOO right now) and @diannakane.

title: Implement server side validations for files only admins can change. I…
Make medic-audit's view generation 8-∞ times faster
body:
# Problem

We are currently having performance problems in LG, **including being unable to write documents.**

This looks to be due to `medic-audit`'s single view taking far too long to generate. While it is a simple view:
- as audit logs get continually larger the efficiency of this view gets worse and worse
- because writing to `medic` must have a successful write to `medic-audit` first
- and because writing to `medic-audit` requires a successful read of the view
- and because a stale view blocks a view read

... we are rejecting writes.
# Fantastic solutions and where to find them
## Allow stale view reads

Difficulty: simple
Improvement: unknown
Caveats: unstable

If we allow for stale view reads for just that view (ie not for the whole DB), it may slightly improve performance, as writes can occur without the view completing generation. **HOWEVER**, this is almost certainly a bad idea, because it may result in multiple audit docs being created for the same document, causing all sorts of madness.

Suggestion: **NOT RECOMMENDED**
## Replace JS view with an Erlang one

Difficulty: simple
Improvement: 7-8x
Caveats: large initial view regen time

Here it is:

``` erlang
fun({Doc}) ->
  case proplists:get_value(<<"type">>, Doc) of
    <<"audit_record">> -> Emit(proplists:get_value(<<"_id">>, Doc), 1)
  end
end.
```

Re-enabling Erlang views, and replacing the existing view with this one, made the view generate 7-8x faster on my laptop (~10000 docs, ~35s vs. 4.5s). I imagine this improvement will increase as the JSON gets larger, because a key performance benefit is dropping JSON parsing.

Suggestion: **GOOD SHORT TERM FIX MAYBE**
## Drop the view completely

Difficulty: moderate
Improvement: ∞
Caveats: requires large migration

We don't actually need the view anymore. Because `medic` and `medic-audit` are separate, and because there is only one audit doc for any given real doc, we can massively simplify the process, and just use the same id for the audit record as we do for the real one. This also makes matching these documents up later more natural as well.

Doing this completely removes the need for a view, which removes the need to generate it, and block on its generation. I presume a direct GET is also much faster than a view query that returns one result, so it's a winner all round.

The obvious downside is that you would need to write a migration script that
- Creates `medic-audit-v2` database
- For each document in `medic-audit`, store it in `medic-audit-v2` with its `_id` changed to that of the document its auditing
- Drop and re-create `medic-audit`
- Replicate `medic-audit-v2` to `medic-audit`
- .... and now medic-api can start

The other downside to note is that you can no longer audit special docs, like ddocs or local docs. I'm not convinced we wanted to audit those anyway tbh, but we really do we could think up a naming convention for them (ie put "audit" in front of the name).

Suggestion: **RECOMMENDED LONG TERM FIX**
## Drop couchdb completely

Difficulty: moderate-high
Improvements: unknown
Caveats: unknown

We could also investigate no longer pushing to couchdb at all. A much simpler solution might be logging to disk an ensuring it's backed up, or picking a different technology that is much more optimal with its writes than its reads.

CouchDB is currently advantageous for us because a) if we ever wanted to access audit docs from the web it would be trivial to do, and b) we already have the dependency in our infrastructure.

Suggestion: **COULD BE LOOKED AT, BUT IMO WE SHOULD STILL DO AN ABOVE IDEA BEFORE THAT**

title: db lib can return `err=undefined, result=undefined`
body:
In sentinel/master the way we handle our db library calls could be improved.  I don't think crashing is really the problem, because the process by design is monitored and restarted and the backlog processing kicks in.  There is no better way atm to reprocess a change (try again) when a dependent resource fails.  But crashing specifically this way on an undefined error is not ideal.  We can throw a more descriptive error like Error("Database returned undefined") or something.

Example of poorly handled db call, these can be found throughout the sentinel code.  We expect `data` to have a `rows` property without checking if data is defined.  When calling our db lib (nano) we should expect both `err` and `data` can be undefined, and just throw a slightly better exception or wrap the calls similar to the [PR against 0.4.x](https://github.com/medic/medic-sentinel/pull/95).  I'm on the fence whether it's better to wrap all the db calls or handle each case where we call nano directly.

title: Add validation option for ISO week date
body:
Per the outcome of #3051, filing a feature request to add validation for ISO week dates to avoid submissions of reports for invalid weeks.

From original issue filed by @bishwas-medic: https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/1423

"ISO week format (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_week_date) and it's variations (WHO uses a similar format called EPID week) are used widely in disease surveillance reporting. Our IPD project(ipd-nepal.app.medicmobile.org) also follows this date format. The reports have a Week number field to identify which ISO week the report is sent for. The max number of weeks in ISO format is either 52 or 53 and currently we are manually updating the validation for the week field to check for wrong weeks using the max() validation.

Having a separate validation like maxISOweek() for checking the week would be a much simpler and better solution to this and can be useful for other areas like analytics dashboards."

title: Support for Nepali number characters
body:
In our projects in Nepal, the reporters have to use the English number for sending numerical values like Weeks since LMP, Days Since Birth, Patient ID in the textforms, while rest of the forms are in Nepali. This is confusing to users and has been a constant cause of errors in reports. Thus the need of support for Nepali numbers.

It is also a major requirement for our government adoption plans for projects, as we are always questioned about the lack of support for the numbers during various meetings and presentation with government agencies and other stakeholders.

Nepali numbers follow the same 10 digit numeral system as the English one and so can be easily mapped 1:1 
```
० -> 0 
१ -> 1
२ -> 2
३ -> 3
४ -> 4
५ -> 5
६ -> 6
७ -> 7
८ -> 8
९ -> 9
```

title: `/api/v1/messages` returns messages twice
body:
`/api/v1/messages` returns each message returned twice. 

That's because the [`tasks_messages` view emits twice per message](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/master/lib/views.js#L439), once to emit the message id and once to emit the message state. Which is because we use the view to query messages both by id and by state.

So for an unfiltered query, we return all view results, which outputs everything twice. 

Either 
 - split that view into two different views (are more views a good thing?), or
 - in the endpoint for `/api/v1/messages`, add a query param of `state=[<all the possible states>]` so that only the `emit`s by state are used and the `emit`s by id are ignored.

title: Make it possible for CHWs to receive SMS notifications when a nurse confirms a visit or delivery via SMS
body:
Currently, when an SMS report is received, the contact information, including the hierarchy of the person who sent the report, is attached. This allows for sending of auto-replies and schedules to the sender and anyone above them in the hierarchy. This works well when the CHW is sending in all of the reports because they can get scheduled messages.

However, we have many nurses in our projects who are currently sending in SMS reports to confirm visits, but the CHW cannot be informed of the nurse's activity. When the nurse sends in a visit report or delivery report, we should be able to send an SMS to that patient's CHW to inform them that the patient went to the clinic.

Now that we have person-centered workflows (and are creating contact docs for all patients), it would be ideal to be able to access the hierarchy info starting from the patient and going up from there as opposed to starting from the person reporting. One thought is that we could attach the contact doc to the SMS report similar to how it is being done for xforms, though we'd only want to do that for person-centered workflows and not for case-based workflows (which are still being supported on v2).

title: Sentinel can make multiple db writes to complete the transitions
body:
Some transitions are order dependant, for example, `update_clinics` sets the contact on the report, then `registration` uses that contact to register the patient. If the contact isn't set then [`registration` is skipped](https://github.com/medic/medic-sentinel/blob/master/transitions/registration.js#L72).

This means if `registration` happens to run first it's skipped, then `update_clinics` and the other transitions run. Then the document is saved which triggers another change. This causes sentinel to check the transitions again and finally `registration` completes and the document is saved a second time.

The end result is the same but saving the document unnecessarily is a performance issue and increases the potential for db conflicts.

Find a way to make all the transitions and save the document in one go.

title: Generate scheduled messages just-in-time so changes to contacts are reflected in yet to be sent messages
body:
For longer-term message schedules, data can easily become stale between the time the schedule is created and the time the scheduled messages are sent. For example, you register a pregnancy today, the EDD is 6 months from now, and messages will be going out for the next 6 months. It's likely the CHW's phone number may change or the name of the mother may be updated in the app during those 6 months. For longer-term use cases, like immunization or growth monitoring, which go on for years, the likelihood is even higher.

We should generate schedules or scheduled messages just-in-time so that they reflect any changes to contacts that may have been made between the time someone is enrolled into a schedule and the time the messages go out.

title: Configurable place hierarchies
body:
Originally reported in #118. Our current hierarchy is limited to 3 levels with hard-coded names. This creates a number of limitations in our deployments, particularly when trying to ensure that users have access to only the data they should/need to have access to. We've been working around this by creatively designing the hierarchy so that it works well enough, but what we really need is more levels to meet our partners' needs.

We should refactor our hierarchy so that every project can have the number of levels that it needs. This is also a precursor to being able to support the roles and permissions that are needed across the different health systems where we work.

Also: not sure how to categorize this feature request, so if anyone has suggestions, let me know! This issue hasn't been scheduled to a release yet.

title: Online-only users never get changes that occured while api was offline
body:
To reproduce:
 - Log in as an admin. Open something you can edit easily (ie a person)
 - Make a change to that person in futon. Note that it automagically updates in the webapp
 - Kill API. Make another change to that person. Boot API back up

What should happen:
Once webapp reconnects to api it should update the UI with the changes

What actually happens:
Nothing! Changes aren't seen until restart / the resource is reloaded.

NB:

This is probably not a problem the majority of the time. The big PITA is that Horticulturalist works by bringing down api, updating the ddoc and bringing it back up. This means with the current system that you don't get notified of the new ddoc, and so don't get asked to refresh.

If it is prohibitive to solve this bug we can probably solve the above problem some other way.

title: Add Horticulturalist integration tests
body:
We have (some) unit test coverage of horti, but we should really do integration tests as well.

There are lots of variables and different ways horti can boot:
 - Are we bootstrapping to some particular version?
 - Are we running in daemon mode or just bootstrapping
 - Do we have an existing deployment / staging deployment on startup
 - Do we already have an existing installation (extracted npm modules) that we should boot first regardless

As well as situations that probably don't matter for when we use this just with medic code, but may matter in the future (or if medic's code changes):
 - What happens if there are no npm modules to deploy
 - What happens if we add / remove an npm module between versions

To enable integration tests we should first:
 - Modify the [build server code](https://github.com/medic/medic-builds-repo) so that it can be pulled from npm, and has a command to "start", which for now is just installing the builds db (far in the future we may need a server in front of this)
 - Modify horti so you can configure an alternative build server from the hard-coded production one

Then, for the integration tests we can first:
 - Wipe / boot a fresh builds "server"
 - Push up a collection of test builds that you can switch between
 - And write tests

This will also conveniently test supporting builds of code that isn't just medic-webapp, and so will probably find bugs.

title: Make bulk importing easier to use
body:
Up till now a developer has always been required to run the `medic-bulk-utils` data imports. For each data set this takes days to execute which is a complete waste of time. We need to make it easy and safe enough for a tech lead or project to use.

This will require some investigation of requirements, but here are some I can think of.

* Performance. The current solution is very slow.
* Robustness. It fails a lot which makes is slower but also error-prone.
* Resumable (if that's a word). If a failure occurs, rerunning should pick up where it left off.

I don't think we need to be flexible in input data format. We can specify one that works for us and leave it up to the user to ensure their data conforms.

It could either be implemented as an API or as part of medic-configurer. Doing it in the API means we can easily wrap a UI around it, and also all the round trip processing happens on the server. Doing it in medic-configurer means you can import to older versions of webapp but that could cause problems where the data structure has changed.

title: Add support for death reporting workflow
body:
This issue adds support for a death reporting and confirmation workflow involving CHWs and managers. We need to support reporting death as well as reversing a death. 

The basic workflow for reporting a death is as follows:

- CHW reports a death in the community via SMS or an app form
- This death report triggers a task for the manager in the app OR sends her an SMS notification
- This task opens a second form (death confirmation) that the manager fills out and submits OR the manager submits a death confirmation form via SMS
- If the manager confirms the death, the person's profile updates to show that they are deceased
- NOTE: The manager can also fill in the death confirmation form directly (in app or via SMS) and the person's profile updates to show that they are deceased

The basic workflow for reversing a death is as follows:

- CHW requests a correction via SMS or an app form
- This request correction form triggers a task for the manager in the app OR sends her an SMS notification
- This task opens an undo death form that the manager submits OR the manager submits an undo death form via SMS
- If the manager confirms that the death should be reversed, the person's profile updates to show that they are alive
- NOTE: The manager can also directly undo the death (in app or via SMS), which should update the profile to show that the person is alive

[Design spec is here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EKmOdip2cebl_BbIJNbl1kTbG3rYxaxVYmI_mL5y9M8/edit#)

Summary of UI changes (these are applied once a death is confirmed). See the design spec for more info:

- [x] person's icon changes from pink to gray (screenshot 1)
- [x] the word "Deceased" is added either next to or immediately below the person's name on their profile (screenshot 1 & 2 are mobile view, on desktop the word "Deceased" should be immediately next to the person's name, see screenshots 6 & 7)
- [x] on the family page, a new row appears at the end of the list of family members that says "View deceased" (screenshot 3)
- [x] when you click on "View deceased", you are taken to a detail page that lists the deceased family members. These are the same as the content rows on the family page except that they show the age at the time of death and have a relative date of death on the right, e.g. "Died 3 years ago" (screenshot 4)
- [x] in search, deceased people should have gray icons and show up at the bottom of the list (screenshot 5)

title: Increase linkages between SMS reports and other docs to streamline analytics queries
body:
Currently, SMS reports have limited information attached to them as this can't be adjusted using config the way it can be for app forms. This causes challenges on the analytics side of things, resulting in complex queries or the inability to calculate certain metrics. This issue will add some linkages between SMS reports and other reports or docs in the DB to help streamline analytics queries.

NOTE: I'm using ANC examples here to illustrate the requests but this should be implemented in a generic way so that it can be used for any use case.

Assumptions:
- N forms are the forms that create new people in the web app
- P forms register pregnancies
- V forms can be any type of visit
- D forms are delivery reports

Linkages to add:
- [x] When an N form is submitted, the person doc that is created should have a `source_id` field with the uuid of the N form that triggered person creation AND a `created_by` field with the uuid of the contact who submitted the N form.
- [x] When a V form is submitted, add a `source_id` field with the uuid of the form that generated the schedule that the V is responding to. For example, if a user sends a P form and then a V form, the V form would have the uuid of the P form on it since the P form generated a schedule.
- [x] When a D form is submitted, add a `source_id` field with the uuid of the form that generated the schedule that the D is responding to. For example, if a user sends a P form, them a V form, then a D form, the D form would have the uuid of the P form.
- [x] Add a `cleared_by` field to any scheduled message that is cleared before it is sent. This field should contain the uuid of the report that cleared the scheduled message.

@michaelkohn is available to provide additional information or talk through scenarios on any of these items.

title: Value for db-doc attribute is case sensitive
body:
With #2912 we can now create a new doc with a report if a group has the attribute `db-doc="true"`. We can set this in XLSForm by having a `instance::db-doc` column, with the group's value set to `true`. However, **setting a field to `true` in Excel can get automatically converted to `TRUE`, which does not create the doc.** 

To get it to stay lower case we should use `'true` in XLSForms.

We should either document this gotcha well and make sure it is well known to anyone building forms, or just accept `TRUE` as an equivalent value. I believe this is checked here: https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/d7eb56c1299d4de7710a1f9f4ea4b8a5babaafee/static/js/services/enketo.js#L383.

title: Have horticulturalist pre-warm views
body:
We should update Horticulturalist so that it takes care of pre-warming views for us. This can be done transparently to users of the system, reducing deployment downtime.

Steps:
 - Remove DDOC extraction from api, and move it into horticultualist. Once it pulls a ddoc down as `medic:staged` it should also extract the other ddocs and name them similarly (ie `medic-cilent:staged` etc).
 - Go through each ddoc in parallel, and use the couchdb api to find one view (any view) and run a limit=1 query against it. If the query times out or fails, retry it. View warming is complete once all ddoc's return the single value from the selected view.
 - Somehow indicate to we're ready to do the ddoc swap (ie change a value somewhere, or use ddoc naming (like `:staged`) in a more complicated way to indicate where in the process we're up to
 - Make sure that the UI can query this days later: i.e., it doesn't require a persistent connection to learn if we're ready to initiate the ddoc swap
 - Change the front-end so that instead of one click to deploy, there are no (sometimes, see discussion) two clicks. The first gets us up to this point and may take some time, the second does the actual deploy
 - Change the horti daemon so that it deploys all extracted ddocs, and not just `medic` , and also kicks off ddoc view cleanup

Q: Should this happen in the api portion of the horti daemon portion? My vote is API, and just leave the horti daemon to manage processes and do the final last section ddoc swapping

Q: How do we want to do the two clicks? Do we want to have it so they must click twice, or that there is some way to only click once (ie just do it, view warming, deploy and all)?

title: Horticulturalist configuration user interface improvements
body:
Dianna and I looked over the page and had some feedback and questions which we posed to Stefan and Alex.

**Here is the biggest issue we would like to solve on this page:**
It sounds like I can only install one of these listed items at a time. But when we see all these "Upgrade" buttons it seems like we would want to "Upgrade" _everything_, which means clicking _all_ the buttons. I'm thinking for instance of when I go in to the app store on my phone, and see that I have 22 items with "Update" next to them - I want to Update everything in the list so everything is current. 

**Ideas for how this could be made clearer:**
- Put everything in a radio button list so you can only select one at a time, with only one big Upgrade button at the bottom of the page 
- Or, what if we at least change the button text to "Install" instead? Install sounds more like something I would only do once.

**A few other suggestions for this page:**
- Increase the space between the text under the "Releases" section and the next title "Betas" and add a horizontal grey line after the text. Why? Right now the "There are no new releases you can upgrade to" message is the key one on this page but it is getting drowned out by the rest of content. Additional white space and the horiz line matches the rest of the page and is a small way to add a little more distinction. 
![screen shot 2017-11-01 at 9 48 23 am](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/32286416-a07ea8aa-beea-11e7-8780-eac491426abd.png)

- Add a label for the middle column describing what the date means
- The red text: Dianna and I were worried the red may be confusing because users have been trained throughout the app to recognize anything red as something that is late (tasks), requires special attention (warnings, high risk etc.), or is performing poorly (targets). An alternative might be changing the color to blue instead, which still stands out on the page but is less bogged down with negative meaning. Alex says the text is red because that is the bootstrap default for code elements. I'm comfortable leaving this decision up to the devs and tech leads as they are most familiar with this page and who will be using it.

title: Deployment containerization: Allow Medic OS components to access Ubuntu base image
body:
We're currently performing a `chroot` inside of the Medic OS Docker image. This is bad for two rreasons: (i) it requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN for bind mounts of `/proc`, `/sys`, and `/dev/pts`, and (ii) it causes Medic OS scripts and binaries to lose access to the binaries and libraries in the base Ubuntu image. We want to remove these restrictions, as it will allow us to "push down" the maintenance of certain services, including security-critical services, into the base image when reliable/maintained packages exist.

Goal: demonstrate a `Dockerfile` build that moves maintenance of OpenSSH out to Ubuntu 16.04 LTS.

Steps:
- [x] Temporarily add `busybox` to Ubuntu base image via Docker
- [x] Audit the `package` and `supervisor` scripts for Ubuntu userspace compatibility
  - [x] Locate uses of Busybox-specific functionality
  - [x] Rewrite, or replace with a backward-compatible invocation of `busybox "$binary"`
- [x] Audit package installation and `run` scripts for Ubuntu userspace compatibility
  - [x] Locate uses of Busybox-specific functionality
  - [x] Rewrite, or replace with a backward-compatible invocation of `busybox "$binary"`
- [x] Attempt full userspace boot, including package installation
  - [x] Locate and fix any remaining errors
- [x] Determine how best to detect the presence of Docker (easy)
- [x] Determine if `busybox` can be removed entirely
- [ ] Modify `openssh` startup script to detect presence of Docker, prefer Ubuntu system-installed binaries and libraries

title: Pull `POST /api/v1/users/{username}` authentication logic out of server.js
body:
Ideally server.js would just be app bootup and routing. We haven't been doing this completely in the past but we should move to it to keep the routing simple.

Traditionally code in `server.js` is where all code that needs to directly muck with `req` and `res` lives, including dealing with specific errors (using `serverUtils`). That code would call through to code in the `/controllers` directory, which uses either callbacks or promises to do logic and return results that don't directly care that they need to be written to HTTP.

The `POST /api/v1/users/{username}` endpoint now has quite a bit of logic in it, because there are multiple ways you are allowed to modify a user. We should move this somewhere else. Probably the best thing long term is to split the current controller into a service and a controller, and have the service doing the logic and the controller managing the relationship between the routing and the service (so the service doesn't care about HTTP primitives but the controller does).

title: Need variable default value for XForm field
body:
In order to get a default value into a field it is possible to use the `default` column in XLSform. This value however is static, and cannot change based on other field values. To have a "variable" default for a text area we are using `calculate`, which worked in Enketo but unlikely supported in base ODK. The calculate would in effect prepopulate the field, which could then be edited by the user. It was used as such in Standard to allow a nurse to edit the "default" message that was to be sent to the CHW -- and that default message would be different based on previous information in the form, and language as well. 

As of `2.13` this method no longer works (as reported by @mukesh2006). Any edits to the text area are not saved with the form, likely since the field's value is recalculated on the page flip as part of https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/3870, overwriting the edits. This can be seen in the form's summary page since it shows the default message, not the edited one. 

We might be able to find another way to do this in the XForm, but would still likely using a non documented bug/feature of the ODK implementation. We should look for, or create, a supported way to do have variable default values.

title: Improve Sentinel performance
body:
**Zerothly**, we should benchmark sentinel, see if we consider it fast enough, and then look at progressively more complex solutions to increase its throughput.

Even without benchmarking (though do this first, maybe it's Good Enough™ already!), Sentinel has some clear places for optimisation.

**Firstly**, it has an intentional 50ms delay in it between processing each document. According to the git log and #907, this was done because sentinel going at [ludicrous speed](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ygE01sOhzz0&feature=youtu.be&t=60) caused CouchDB to freeze and become unstable. We should investigate how true this is, and why. Is this still true with CouchDB 2.0? Is this just because of lots of individual writes? Or is this a combination of writes and view regenerations in between those writes? If a delay really is required, is there a small value that we could use (it used to be 500ms!)? Is there another metric entirely other than "arbitrary sleep time" that we could use to maintain stability? Answering these questions will help determine some larger solutions.

**Secondly**, there are a couple of places: `deleteInfoDoc` and `deleteReadDocs`; which could be converted into asynchronous queues[1] instead of their actions blocking more processing. These may not be run that much, because they only run when a document is deleted, so it might not be worth the code change effort.

**Thirdly**, there are a couple of different easy strategies for improving performance that don't require re-architecting much. Both strategies I'm about to describe would require we add some kind of `partition` function (other name ideas: `index`, `groupBy`) to the transition api, which each transition would implement. `partition` would be a function that would return, given a document, a value which is used to describe how to group / categorise the action the transition performs on that document. This can then be used to try to increase performance:
 1. Increase throughput by increasing the number of queues we have, from one to as many queues as we have unique values from `partition`. 
 2. Reduce writes by putting writes into a queue, and not writing until we're going to process a document for which there is already the same `partition` value in the queue.

The current thought about the implementation of `partition` is that for most things it would be the patient id, or perhaps the chw's / contact's uuid. However, for some transitions it would be a constant value (eg the transition's name), to force concurrency inside that transition. The clearest example being multi report alerts (after you see N things send a message: this cannot be parallelised without re-writing the transition and probably the transition processing flow).

So in the first approach we will be writing document from two CHPs concurrently, while still maintaining ordering inside those CHPs. And in the second example, we would delay writing until we were trying to process a document for a CHP for which we already have a queued write. The first approach will smash CouchDB harder, the second would smash CouchDB less. Which approach is best (or even deciding to do both) is dependent on the modern reasoning behind the 50ms delay.

**Fourthly**, and similarly to the previous point, we could look at relationships between one transition and all others, and itself. We could do this to categorise transitions and work out which ones can be parallelised without trouble, and which rely on others (can't accept patient reports before the registration is processed) or itself (multi-report-alerts, as described above). It's not clear if this individual action is more useful than just mostly doing it in the third point though.

**Lastly**, it's time to give up the idea that you can just re-write bits of sentinel, and we have look at a whole new architecture. Yikes.

[1] With all queues that is we talk about in this doc, we'd expect that: they are disk-backed; pick up queued items on re-boot, and where relevant flush after N seconds regardless. Once we add queues we'd also need to make sure the "seq we're up to" flow works properly, as that would be disrupted by this kind of thing.

title: Improve the filtered replication algorithm
body:
The current algorithm has increased our replication performance significantly but has a few issues.

- [ ] In order to get notified of deletions we pass the list of IDs that PouchDB knows about. This does not scale. Find a better way to get deletion changes. More info on #4172
- [ ] Up until recently it had a timing issue where new docs could be skipped during replication if a change happened at the same time. Unfortunately the fix for this bug requires four database view requests every time the change handler fires which will hurt performance. We should find a better way of reliably getting every change. More info on #4166 
- [ ] It has no integration or e2e testing. It's a critical piece of our functionality so we need to ensure we don't regress when we make improvements.
- [ ] It is complicated and monolithic which makes it hard to read and understand and also hard to unit test for because you end up having to mock too much.

Notes:

- It may be useful to split the concept of catchup/initial replication from the continuous waiting replication. For example, for catchup replication it's highly performant to determine all the IDs a user is allowed to see and pass that to the CouchDB changes request. However with waiting replication this algorithm exposes #4166
- It may be useful to split the concept of deletions from the replication altogether as our current method of getting IDs you're allowed to see via a view means we don't know which deleted docs you _were_ allowed to see. This would be one way to solve #4172 
- Alternatively we could permanently store all the IDs you've ever been allowed to see and use that to request the changes feed.
- For waiting replication we currently make at least one changes request per longpoll request each with their own set of doc IDs. It may be more efficient to make one request for all changes including docs and run our own filter function and then respond to the relevant feeds. This would reduce load on CouchDB but add it to API.

title: Consider re-writing (C|P)ouchDB pagination without skip and limit
body:
Generally when we do pagination we use skip / limit:
 - Do a query with skip:0, limit: N
 - Do things with those N results
 - If < N results then you're done
 - Other loop, with skip = skip + N

This is really easy, and works everywhere, but it has performance problems: http://docs.couchdb.org/en/latest/ddocs/views/pagination.html

We should consider understanding this and rewriting some pagination that we do.

The most obvious places to look at fixing would the search shared library, and some migrations. Searching the code for `skip: ` is pretty illuminating.

title: IDs of new documents are not added to changes requests until page refresh
body:
To replicate:
 - Open a restricted user, watch the network. You should generate a longpoll _change request once everything is synced.
 - Create a new document. Note that a bunch of stuff happens on the network, but specifically that the first longpoll is satisfied by the document you just created, and a new longpoll is created after this.
  - Do that a few more times for good effect.
  
What should happen:
 - Every time a new longpoll request is initiated after you write a document, the id of that document should be among the ids passed

What actually happens:
 - The ids are the same each time.
 - If you refresh the longpoll that is initiated after this has the correct doc ids. 

Looking at the code this is actually obvious: we only add the doc_ids when we're instantiating the two way sync the first time.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/36556416-1a08a6d0-17d3-11e8-9e44-2da1d7d2dced.png)

# Date is shown as off by one, depending on your timezone
The date is a day earlier than expected, likely due to a timezone issue (https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/488). The calculated date for the date of birth is `"birth_date":"2018-02-22T00:00:00.000Z"`, therefore we are assuming that all SMS are submitted on UTC. When seeing this date in EST (as in my case) it shows the birthday as being a day off. 

- **Should we instead save the day without the time component eg `2018-02-22` ?**

# Relative date + time is misleading
The relative date/time resolution should match the date resolution. It seems odd to say "18 hours" ago for an event that was "today". If the birth date is a day, we should only have relative we could have "today", "days/weeks/months/years ago", but not "hours ago"

**Would this automatically be resolved if the date were saved without the time component as mentioned above?**

------
There is a larger question of how to take into account timezones in message scheduling. That seems like a separate but relevant issue, and one we will run into more as we projects further away from UTC. @henokgetachew, how are we currently dealing with this now?

title: Refactor messages_by_contact_date view to reduce more
body:
The `medic-client/messages_by_contact_date` view is designed to return an object which contains all the information needed for the message list reduced to show only the last message from each contact. As the amount of information needed has increased so has the emitted value which means sometimes it crashes because the reduce isn't reducing the size of the object as much as expected (#4101). To get around this we introduced some message truncation so long messages wouldn't break, but this is buggy with unicode characters and also makes the view code unnecessarily complicated.

Refactor this to return just the `reported_date` as the value and reduce to find the latest message. Then on the client side get all the IDs of the latest messages and fetch the docs in a separate request. This is slightly worse client side performance (two requests instead of one) but much easier on the server view generator and will always reduce the output enough to avoid the error. It also means we don't need to do message truncation we can just rely on the css ellipsis overflow.

title: Gardener repeatedly scans every db looking for modules to install
body:
While testing the upgrade from 2.12 to 2.14, I noticed that view indexing was taking a long time and seemed to be failing repeatedly and re-starting. Upon closer inspection, @garethbowen realized that now that we have 1 db per user, gardener is scanning through all of these dbs repeatedly, as fast as it can, looking for modules to install, which is quite bad for performance. This may need an update to medic-os.

Unfortunately, this is a blocker for the 2.14.0 release.

This is because these fields are now translated as part of the .properties files, which only show in the `Application text` tab. 

A couple of possible options:
1) Remove the `Outgoing messages` tab altogether. _Simple, but removes existing functionality for older configs with text in app_settings._
1) Hide the tab if there are no labels that would show. _Same as 1 above, but only if there are no translations in app_settings._
1) Hide the items that don't have editable translations. _Similar to 2, but instead hide items don't have translations in app_settings_
1) Bring the appropriate labels into the Outgoing messages tab. _Preserves the functionality of editing translations for outgoing messages, and separating them from the long list of other labels_

I would think that the last option is ideal from a user perspective, if it is not substantially more effort.

title: Write integration tests against lineage
body:
Looking at a lot of the current unit tests for lineage, I'm not convinced they test what they say they are testing. In general these tests are very complicated as they require correctly mocking multiple ordered DB calls. For complete correctness they should also validate that the calls are actually the right ones (ie the query provides the right params),  which no / few tests do. For this reason it's also really hard to write new tests, because you have to walk the whole codebase and work out what to mock and when.

We need to be able to write integration tests for lineage. This is only complex because lineage relies on the ddocs existing:
 - Work out how to get the current ddocs in testing. This could be as simple as the tests actually understanding where they are in the file hierarchy and calling the code that generates the ddocs (once kanso is removed), and taking the resulting files off the fs and uploading them to a local PouchDB. This sounds gross, but is OK because testing!
 - The just write mocha tests that don't mock anything, and use a local PouchDB (in-memory is fine, or write to disk)

This would actually prove the code is working, as well as making sure if we ever change these views the code continues to work against them.

title: TIMEOUT errors watching changes feed For Some Reason™
body:
I've noticed this over the past few weeks, it at least affects 2.15+, though could be affecting 2.14 as well. It's really easy to tell, just log in as an admin (restricted might also cause this problem) and watch the network log in chrome tools.

You get lots of errors in changes feed watching:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/583851/37707446-049708b8-2cfb-11e8-96ef-f60e0760e359.png)
Which when you look in the network log are cancellations because of stalling after 15 seconds:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/583851/37707460-1660f694-2cfb-11e8-970f-a793cc6dc3f1.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/583851/37707475-2493e41a-2cfb-11e8-9fbe-35615f3b17cc.png)
Stalling, according to: https://developers.google.com/web/tools/chrome-devtools/network-performance/reference#timing-explanation
> Stalled. The request could be stalled for any of the reasons described in Queueing.
> Queueing. The browser queues requests when:
> - There are higher priority requests.
> - There are already six TCP connections open for this origin, which is the limit. Applies to HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 only.
> - The browser is briefly allocating space in the disk cache

The middle one is perhaps the most likely.

This doesn't cause any noticeable problem for users, but effectively means we hold the connection open for 15 seconds and then reestablish, which seems like a waste.

body:
Currently, online users are (on semi-large instances) unusable because:
 - The `_changes` feed watching in the `Changes` service watches and downloads every change to the database in full (eg `include_docs: true`)
 - The UI then live-responds based on the page you're on and updates accordingly (changing the value of a form, adding / removing reports from the LHS etc)

On semi-large instances this is both way to much data to constantly download, and way too many UI updates to be performant.

NB: this is still fine for offline users, as they don't see as much data, and they already need the data on their device anyway.

Instead, we should:
 - Go through all usages of the `Changes` service and work out how to replace the functionality in a minimal way. For example, LHS lists should have a button you can press to refresh the search (this may already work this way).
 - If each usage can be replaced in a nice way make those changes and disable the Changes service for online users.
 - If there are instances where we still need some kind of change watching (detecting an upgrade comes to mind) we may need to build a less generic / more efficient changes service that we can use to know if there are new pieces of information for a particular view / use case, but not the whole contents until eg. someone refreshes. This would be in api. We can cross that bridge if we feel like we come to it.

title: Write a doc minification script to apply migrations to a running instance
body:
Over the last couple of years we've made some changes to how we store data to reduce disk space requirements and/or improve performance, however because the migrations would take a long time to run we decided to make the changes in a backwards compatible way. Unfortunately that means existing documents are unoptimised.

Write a script to execute database optimisations against a running instance.

Optimisations to consider including are...

- minifying contacts
- storing report xml in an attachment
- removing read data which has been migrated into the user db
- anything else you can think of

Features the script could include are...

- run only between certain times each day (overnight, over the weekend, etc) - it will need to remember which docs have been processed in previous executions
- run against certain branches only so individual CHPs download all their changes in one go rather than a couple of changes a day
- throttling so it doesn't lock the server up

The first project this script will be executed against will be LG so follow up with @derickl with any questions.

**EDIT**

Original issue below. The "real" problem is that angular.bootstrap takes forever to bootstrap our app. See: https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/4422#issuecomment-382016062

---

The move from the specific counted replication step (which is super awesome and makes it clear something is happening) to the generic "we're doing the loads now" label happens after server -> client replication but *not* after client -> server replication. If you recall, this is it checking with the server to see if the server needs the documents it just replicated down (which is silly, but that's the current couchdb protocol so let's run with it).

We should either have another step ("Syncing info (yyy docs)"?), or count the sync from client -> server as part of that doc count, and don't end the counting until both server -> client and client -> server are complete.

I think this would increase user confidence in initial app load.

title: Optimise form HTML generation
body:
Currently phones regenerate the HTML for a form every time the browser is refreshed. This slows down first time form loading by a second or two on most phones.

Instead, we should cache this generation more aggressively somehow.

Probably the most complete solution would be to actually ship the HTML to devices instead of the form xml, and then generate the HTML in either sentinel or as part of upload in medic-conf.

We have to be careful because there are quite a few things in play:
 - form version
 - enketo version
 - our custom xslt versions
 - potentially general app version (in case we change / add feature sets)
 - other things?? (jquery version? other libraries that we utilise?)

FWIW I tried to do it in browser, by storing the generated HTML in a `_local/formCache` document. It presented many challenges, chief among ironically keeping general form requests as fast as a dumb in-memory cache:
 - You need to check lots of things when you boot to make sure nothing has changed out from under you
 - You can't check form version (or other things) every time a form is asked for because that is too slow: it has to just be pulling the cache from memory and looking at keys
 - So you need to attach a follow to the changes feed and selectively wipe parts of the cache dependent on what comes through on that
 - Understanding that this follow might not be set up in time as replication starts before you get a chance to attach so you need to make your initial boot logic (first point) as specific as this one
 - And also probably understand whether or not you're admin, because writing to a remote `_local` makes no sense (or _does it!?!?!_), so do you then write to a local local (which admins don't have), or for admins do you just back on to the existing style of memory cache?

title: Bulk delete errors on conflict
body:
Raised from #4113 

The bulk delete should make sure that when it's done all documents that were asked to be deleted are deleted.

Currently this can fail to be true if there are conflicts, which not only stops the conflicted documents from being deleted, but also halt the bulk delete completely.

One solution would be to take conflicts and add those documents to the end of the queue to be retried later.

title: Cannot send multiple scheduled messages at same time
body:
As seen in https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/4453#issuecomment-385440778, messages from a group cannot be sent at the same time. Only one message per group goes from `scheduled` to `pending` when [due_tasks.js](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/ba2715130682cf6f7cd60b15868c1a57a4824304/sentinel/schedule/due_tasks.js) is run (every 5 minutes).

This can lead to puzzling behaviour, as seen below, where scheduled messages are not going to `pending` when you may expect them to:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/39436941-7455b3b6-4c6d-11e8-9b7c-2bf139530285.png)

We should decide if this is a bug that needs to be fixed, otherwise document accordingly.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Upload a config with multiple scheduled messages going out at the same time, or within a 5 minute span.
1. Submit a form that triggers the schedule.
1. Observe the `scheduled` time vs `pending` time for each message.

## What should happen
All scheduled messages should go from `scheduled` to `pending` within 5 minutes of the scheduled sending time.

## What does happen
If there is more than one message that should go to pending in a 5 minute span only the first one goes to `pending`. The others go to pending one at a time every subsequent 5 minutes.

title: Add ability to sort places by date last visited
body:
This feature makes it easier for CHWs to identify households they have not visited recently so that they can ensure every household is visited each month.

Currently, the list of places on the people tab is sorted alphabetically. This feature adds the ability to sort by the date the place was last visited. The date the place was last visited is determined by the `reported_date` of a form submitted at the place level. When places are sorted by date last visited, the place visited longest ago is at the top, with those visited most recently at the bottom. This allows the user to prioritize visits with places visited the longest ago. If the date last visited is unknown, this should be at the very top of the list, above the longest ago date known. The default sort should still be Alphabetically.

Open question for discussion: will adding this sort apply to all hierarchy levels? Or only the lowest level? Or would we be able to select which levels it would apply to?

Additional requirement: this feature is part of "universal health coverage" (UHC) mode, which is a group of features we'd like to be able to toggle on and off (either using configuration, feature flags, user permissions, or some other solution). More information about UHC mode in #4525.

UI components:
- [x] clear search icon moves next to the search box
- [x] new icon for sort is added to the right of the clear search icon (16px, fa-sort-amount-desc, same color as other icons)
- [x] clicking on the sort icon pops up a white box with 4px rounded corners and drop shadow
- [ ] the white box has title Sort this list (16px bold, 20px from the left edge)
- [ ] below the title are two options: Alphabetically and By date last visited (16px, 40px from left edge)
- [ ] whichever option is selected has a green checkmark next to it (16px, fa-check, #8EB41D)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1286381/39655345-edacc810-4fad-11e8-9004-f6d52161b725.png) ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1286381/39655409-4d3185e6-4fae-11e8-98ed-00cf035cdd0b.png)

More details [in this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1y5g_Oi4a-3pQbwwTwPEsWX0jF7AJML2lnH9XsVhb_yA/edit#).

Acceptance criteria:
- clicking on the sort icon pops up a white box of appropriate size/location
- sorting by date last visited sorts the list so that unknown dates are at the top, followed by the longest ago dates and then the most recent dates are at the bottom
- sorting alphabetically sorts the list alphabetically

title: Make it possible to toggle universal health coverage mode on and off
body: As we are developing the first few features for our universal health coverage (UHC) mode, we would like to solidify the concept of these features as a mode for our app that can be toggled on and off. If UHC mode is on, the user should have the ability to sort by date last visited (#4524) and should see the date last visited listed for each place instead of the primary contact (#4526). In the future, turning UHC mode on might include more features, or we may end up making it the default mode for our application. For now, as long as we have a way (configuration, feature flags, user permissions, etc.) to turn the features on and off, that will accomplish the goal of this ticket.

title: Replace the primary contact with date last visited in the people list
body:
This feature makes it easier for CHWs to see when they last visited a particular household.

Currently, the list of places on the people tab shows the primary contact for each place. In the list of households, this information is often repetitive as the household is named after its primary contact. This feature replaces that information with the date last visited. The date the place was last visited is determined by the `reported_date` of a form submitted at the place level. 

The date last visited should be displayed as a relative date. If none of the forms that generate the date have been submitted, the date should be listed as unknown. If the last visit date is one month ago or more, the text should be red to call attention to it. "One month" is 30 days in this case, not the previous calendar month.

Open question for discussion: will displaying the date apply to all hierarchy levels? Or only the lowest level? Or would we be able to select which levels it would apply to?

Additional requirement: this feature is part of "universal health coverage" (UHC) mode, which is a group of features we'd like to be able to toggle on and off (either using configuration, feature flags, user permissions, or some other solution). More information about UHC mode in #4525.

UI components:
- [x] date last visited is in the exact same place and is the exact same size as the primary contact
- [x] if the date is one month ago or more, the font color changes to red (no other styling changes)
- [x] if the date is unknown, the font color changes to red (no other styling changes)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1286381/39657020-fc2ac0c6-4fb8-11e8-8f03-2856cb838039.png)

More details [in this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1y5g_Oi4a-3pQbwwTwPEsWX0jF7AJML2lnH9XsVhb_yA/edit#heading=h.wvrlt93yb7dw).

Acceptance criteria:
- date last visited listed for each place
- unknown dates are listed in red
- dates more than one month ago are listed in red

title: Horticulturalist restart behavior
body:
We need to work out, confirm and potentially fix restart behaviour, at least while deployed under MedicOS, but ideally locally as well.

I think this is how it works now:

Under MedicOS:
 - Horti is started by the OS, and does not automatically start any packages
 - The packages are started by the OS
 - If any of the packages die, they are restarted independently by the OS
 - If Horti dies, horti will be restarted and I *think* the packages will attempt to be started, but it should be fine because they are already started

Locally:
 - Horti is started by the user
 - Horti starts any packages itself 
 - If Horti is closed cleanly via CTRL+C Horti and any packages are killed
 - If Horti crashes / is uncleanly closed (eg kill) packages are (annoyingly) left running
 - If a package crashes it is not restarted

The one super obvious bug is if horti gets "uncleanly" terminated packages don't die, which is a massive pita because you have to grep for node processes to manually kill them.

Apart from that, two big questions come from this:
 - Are the MedicOS behaviours acceptable for production?
 - What would we want to happen locally if a package dies? Should we restart the package, kill everything, or leave it alone?

          "progress": 82,
          "started_on": 1527075166,
          "total_changes": 2942,
          "type": "indexer",
          "updated_on": 1527075186
        },
        {
          "node": "couchdb@localhost",
          "pid": "<0.8072.326>",
          "changes_done": 2424,
          "database": "shards/80000000-ffffffff/medic.1525076838",
          "design_document": "_design/:staged:medic-client",
          "indexer_pid": "<0.9817.326>",
          "progress": 81,
          "started_on": 1527075166,
          "total_changes": 2967,
          "type": "indexer",
          "updated_on": 1527075186
        }
      ]
    },
```

We currently just output `design_document` and `progress`.

We could make this much nicer:
 - Have it sort in a way that makes sense
 - Either combine output from multiple shards / nodes (the setup in the picture has two shards on one node) into one average %, or change the output so that it's clear that you're looking at a specific node/shard combination
 - Make the code that updates `indexers` smarter, so that once an indexer disappears it marks it's progress as 100% complete instead of it just disappearing.

There are probably lots of different ways we could display this smarter. As long as it's clear what is going on and progress doesn't just disappear once complete it would be an improvement.

title: Reduce how long horticulturalist takes node modules down for
body:
Horti does a lot of work in the background before it restarts api and sentinel, but there is even more we can move out from between restarts.

Take a look at the current process: https://github.com/medic/horticulturalist/blob/master/src/install/deploySteps.js

The process from stopping to starting should really just be:
 - Stop processes
 - Move staged ddocs into production locations
 - Change symlink from old node_module locations to new ones
 - Start processes

Currently we also:
 - Extract new node_modules from staged ddocs
 - Write them to disk
 - Clean up and delete old node modules from disk

The first two bullet points should be done before processes are stopped, and the last one should be done in the existing cleanup phase.

This improvement changes how we are using the red or green dot in the reports list and on the report detail page. More specifically, it changes the meaning of the green dot from "valid" to "verified/correct", and allows the red dot to be applied to reports submitted via the app in cases where they are marked as "has errors" (see #4529).

- [ ] a red dot with an x in it should appear for any invalid SMS reports
- [ ] a red dot with an x in it can be applied to an app report if that report has errors (see #4529)
- [ ] a green dot with a checkmark in it can be applied to an app report if that report is valid/correct (see #4529)

title: Allow supervisors to access specific patient reports so that they can review them
body:
For the Muso IN, we are planning to deploy a workflow where a supervisor needs to review all patient assessments that included an mRDT test. The CHW will be taking a photo of the mRDT test to upload with the patient assessment and the supervisor needs to review the photo to check whether or not the CHW read the result of the test correctly. Since the Muso supervisors are restricted users, they do not have access to all people and all reports about those people. This ticket would allow the supervisor to access reports about patients that meet certain conditions. In this case, it would be patient assessment forms in which an mRDT test was administered.

Requirements:
- Supervisors have to be able to see the photos and the result that the CHW reported after reading the test within a patient assessment form (there are multiple patient assessment forms, one for children and one for adults)
- Supervisors need to be able to use the feature built in #4529 to review the patient assessment form and mark if the result was read correctly or incorrectly
- The CHW needs to know if their result was read correctly or incorrectly because they need to see a target widget that displays their error rate (number or percent of reports marked incorrect/has errors)
- If possible, the supervisor would like to see the error rate for each CHW on that CHW's profile in the supervisor's view of the app

Acceptance criteria:
- When a CHW submits a report with an mRDT photo, the required information successfully replicates to the supervisor's tablet
- After the supervisor marks the report as correct or incorrect, the CHW's error rate target widget updates correctly and the CHW's profile card (as seen by the manager) updates to display the latest error rate

@garethbowen let me know if I've omitted anything from our discussion.

title: Allow registration with age in months or years
body:
Incoming forms can currently specify an age in **days** or **weeks**, and set the date of birth on the doc accordingly. It would be useful for Standard deployments to be able to specify the age in **months**.

The original immunization workflow required registration of children up to 2 years old, which was feasible by specifying the age in weeks. With the [new child health workflow](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/4155) you can register children up to 5 years old for messages -- which makes registring with age in weeks quite difficult.

Age in years in not needed for Standard (yet), although could be useful for some use cases (eg registration of pregnant women).

cc @jillrshah, @ranjuts

title: Message's translation key sent when translation is missing
body:
If a translation is missing for a scheduled message's translation key, we are currently sending the key itself as the SMS. Instead we should make sure to not send a message at all.

As part of the [Standard Child Health messaging](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/4155) we are setting up 60 months worth of monthly messages. If we decide at a later time to send messages only every second month, we would configure the schedule for new registrations accordingly. For existing registrations we would want to be able to blank out the messages that should not go out. We could most easily do that by setting the corresponding translations to blank, or remove them altogether. 

Setting messages to blank seems like a quicker solution than recalculating the entire schedule for previous schedules, and this method can buy us time until the messages are generated on the fly by a rules engine.

Here is an example of a report that has a message pending with the translation key as the message:
```
	"scheduled_tasks": [{
		"due": "2018-06-03T19:27:03.551Z",
		"group": 1,
		"type": "Child_Health",
		"translation_key": "schedule.child_health",
		"message_key": "messages.schedule.child.month_00",
		"recipient": "clinic",
		"state_history": [{
			"state": "scheduled",
			"timestamp": "2018-06-03T19:25:09.804Z"
		},
		{
			"state": "pending",
			"timestamp": "2018-06-03T19:31:00.542Z"
		}],
		"state": "pending",
		"messages": [{
			"uuid": "4a130a0e-386a-4f5d-9d2f-5c50f674aa1b",
			"to": "+14165551230",
			"message": "messages.schedule.child.month_00"

title: Allow translation to nest another translation key
body:
As mentioned in #4598:
> as part of the [Standard Child Health messaging](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/4155) we are setting up 60 months worth of monthly messages. 

We are setting separate translation keys for each to allow independent changes to each month's message. For now there are three different messages that are repeated 8, 20, and 32 times. To avoid bloating the translations we should allow specifying a translation key within a translation.

For instance, we may want to do something like this:
```properties
month_01 = This is a monthly message
month_02 = ${month_01}
```

title: Make family equity score available for family member task generation and within forms about family members
body:
This feature makes the family equity score available within forms about family members or for generating or updating task schedules for family members. Equity scores can be collected either during family registration or via a form filled in at the family/household level. The scores might impact the frequency at which a CHW should visit a particular household or require the CHW to follow a different pregnancy visit schedule for women in households with lower scores.

The equity score is a measure of wealth. By asking questions about housing materials, possessions, and a few other things, the survey determines which wealth quintile a family falls into. Being in a lower quintile might mean you are less likely to deliver at a health facility or less likely to seek treatment when you are sick. Using these scores to help target households is important in making sure that CHWs can provide equitable care.

Equity scores are somewhat static, but they might be re-evaluated every 6 months or so (schedule would vary by project).

Requirements:
- Equity score for the family is available in forms about all family members
- Equity score for the family can be used to determine task schedules for family members

Acceptance criteria:
- Can access equity score in person-level forms
- Can use equity score to trigger a different task schedule if the score is above/below a certain threshold

title: Reports page can mistakenly hide fields
body:
A submitted report may be have fields hidden that should be shown.

**Steps to reproduce**:
 - Write a form with a hidden field whose name is the prefix to another field, or use the one included below
 - Submit that report

**What should happen**:
 - Only the specific field that is marked with `tag="hidden"` should be hidden. In this case it is the `name` field.

**What actually happens**:
 - All fields that start with the same name as the intended hidden field are hidden. In the example below `name2` is greedily hidden, and shouldn't be.

Tested on version 2.14.3


## Example XForm
```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<h:html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2002/xforms" xmlns:ev="http://www.w3.org/2001/xml-events" xmlns:h="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:jr="http://openrosa.org/javarosa" xmlns:orx="http://openrosa.org/xforms" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <h:head>
    <h:title>Issue: Hidden Fields</h:title>
    <model>
      <instance>
        <hidden_fields delimiter="#" id="hidden_fields" prefix="J1!hidden_fields!" version="2018-06-12 22-55">
          <name tag="hidden"/>
          <name2/>
          <another_name/>
        </hidden_fields>
      </instance>
      <instance id="contact-summary"/>
      <bind nodeset="/hidden_fields/name" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/hidden_fields/name2" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/hidden_fields/another_name" type="string"/>
    </model>
  </h:head>
  <h:body>
    <input ref="/hidden_fields/name">
      <label>name</label>
    </input>
    <input ref="/hidden_fields/name2">
      <label>name2</label>
    </input>
    <input ref="/hidden_fields/another_name">
      <label>another_name</label>
    </input>
  </h:body>
</h:html>
```

**Snippet of doc for a submitted report**
```json
{
  "hidden_fields":["name"],
  "fields":{
    "name":"i",
    "name2":"i2",
    "another_name":"i3"
  }
}
```

title: relativeDays filter only shows days, not months etc (unlike relativeDate)
body:
To replicate, mucking around with the code is probably the easiest to see the change.

We have two relative time filters that we can use to output relative time based on an absolute time: `relativeDay` and `relativeDate`. From current usage and the code it looks like the intention is that one of them shows relative time including times earlier than "today", and the other does not. e.g. `relativeDate` would show "13 minutes ago" while `relativeDay` would just show "today".

However, there is also another difference that I think is unintentional: the largest time period `relativeDay` seems to support is days. That means it will output "55 days ago", as opposed to "2 months ago" like `relativeDate` would.

To me, the only difference between the two should be the minimum sized time period (seconds for `relativeDate`, days for `relativeDay`) and not the maximum.

title: Improve death reporting workflow by allowing the death confirmation form to specify the date of death
body:
Currently, when the `death_reporting` transition runs, it adds a `date_of_death` field to the contact doc that is equal to the `reported_date` of the death confirmation form. However, the death confirmation is likely to happen after the actual date of death. We'd like to provide a way to indicate the date of death in the death confirmation form so that the date of death that is recorded on the contact doc is the actual date of death.

@garethbowen suggested that the death confirmation form can include a field called `date_of_death` that would be saved on the contact doc. If not, the transition could fall back on the death confirmation report's `reported_date`.

title: Enable response body compression
body:
Old medic-os instances had gzip compression enabled in nginx, but Docker instances don't have nginx and compression is no longer happening. This can be enabled in express but [it's better to implement it at a reverse proxy level](https://expressjs.com/en/advanced/best-practice-performance.html#use-gzip-compression).

This is a blocker for using Docker in production.

title: Use asynchronous logging in node apps
body:
`console.*` synchronously blocks so is not recommended for production deployments. The express documentation [recommends using logging libraries](https://expressjs.com/en/advanced/best-practice-performance.html#do-logging-correctly) instead.

Replace all existing console invocations and implement a precommit regex check similar to the ones that exist for the webapp to ensure no new calls are added.

title: Performance issues loading contacts
body:
Querying the `doc_summaries_by_id` view is _really_ slow. On my Tecno with about 300 docs it takes about 4 seconds just to query the db (ignore rendering, setup, etc). PouchDB is making individual allDocs requests for each of the docs rather than one bulk get. 

I modified the GetDataRecords service to replace the view query with an allDocs request and shaved 2 seconds off the fetch time. If this change is also made for the other queries in the stack I expect to shave another 2 seconds or so off the request making it complete almost immediately.

GetDataRecords is used on the Reports tab too (and maybe other places) so performance improvements here could have broad implications.

Work out why PouchDB is doing so badly, and either fix it or implement the above workaround.

title: Translate our startup messages for non-English speakers
body:
People who do not have English as their primary language find our startup messages ("Loading assets", "Fetching Info (100 docs)..." etc) very confusing.

We do not currently translate these because angular has not yet started, and so we do not have the translation service yet. If this is the very first run we would also not have their language, because it wouldn't be the cookie yet, and we wouldn't have their user document yet.

Do we have any ideas on what we could do here to make this less confusing for users? The two most obvious options would be:
 - Add minimal translation support: hard code different languages, also load the user's context document if it doesn't already exist to make sure we get the language
 - Change what is rendered so it works across languages and cultures without requiring people have a firm grasp of english.

I think the former is easier but a bit more hacky (we'd now have translations in two places, but it's pretty contained and isn't that large of a deal IMO), and the latter is probably better, but much harder and would require a large amount of design work

title: Remove blank UI elements in Enketo forms
body:
In `2.16.0-beta.7` we have a lot of unexpected blank lines in Enketo forms for Standard:

## Actual layout
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/42116335-c42d232a-7bc4-11e8-9663-9f652755d2cb.png)

## Desired layout
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/42116292-9ed60a4c-7bc4-11e8-82ea-324fef94b123.png)

## Notes
- The XForm converter tool pyxform requires labels for groups
- We remove the label text in medic-conf if it is `NO_LABEL`
- These labels are still taking vertical space, even if they are blank.
- Sample form is [here](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/1403c371e5a693618817d21ebc73f49814ede26b/config/standard/forms/contact/district_hospital-create.xml).

Seems as though the ideal solution would be to remove the actual label, and avoid having blank definitions. This would likely be best done in `medic-conf`.

## Current XForm
Currently we have one of the following for every language in the model:
```
          <text id="/data/district_hospital:label">
            <value></value>
          </text>
```

The label is actually blank but in the UI body:

```
    <group appearance="field-list" ref="/data/district_hospital">
      <label ref="jr:itext('/data/district_hospital:label')"/>
      <group ref="/data/district_hospital/contact">
```

## Ideal XForm

Same as before but with no blank definitions in the model, and no empty UI element in the body:
```
    <group appearance="field-list" ref="/data/district_hospital">
      <group ref="/data/district_hospital/contact">

```

title: Create a shared library for server startup checks
body: We have a bunch of code in api/server.js and sentinel/server.js which checks certain prerequisites (eg: node version, logging env.NODE_OPTIONS) before starting. This is duplicated but also gets out of sync if new checks are added to one and not the other. Create a shared library with all the checks that both services should run.

title: Make debugging harder to leave on
body:
On the About page we have an option to turn on debugging. This sets a cookie which is checked on startup and if set sets angular and pouchdb to log everything. This is useful for development but should never be left on in a production environment because it slows down the app significantly and blows out feedback docs (related: #4481). I also have trouble turning it off and getting it to stay off suggesting that the cookie deletion code isn't working. We're getting [reports from the field](medic/medic-projects#4343) which indicate some users have this turned on so it's a problem in the wild.

1. Decide whether we want debugging to be sticky - perhaps it should just stay on until refresh, or maybe it should only be sticky in development mode.
2. Consider disabling debugging altogether in a production environment.
3. Work out how to make sure turning debugging off actually disables it after refresh.
