title: PouchDB replication _bulk_get is no longer batched
body:
Since the upgrade to PouchDB 7.0.0 (in 3.1.0), Webapp _bulk_get replication calls are no longer batched.
The specific update that causes this is [this commit](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/commit/2987c56311ae2d170d7c1d856470894f760a819a#diff-39bf4acf1588841b5eb6168b8bd48e0d), which changes the moment the `onChange` event is emitted (instead of a sequential emit, which allowed the replicator to batch, events for all changes are emitted at once and processing happens on `nextTick`). 

This causes replication to consist of one `_changes` request which, as before, will return all changes (since the beginning of time for initial replication), regardless of the limit PouchDB sets, one `_all_docs` request for changed docs that are on first rev and one `_bulk_get` request for all the other changes. 

This means a potential `_bulk_get` to get thousands of docs. 
@garethbowen do you think this could be a problem?

title: Client-side Purging
body:
For your consideration.

I spent a couple of hours today knocking out the basics of purge on the phone:
 - Runs every N days on refresh (in my hard-coded configuration I have it at 0 so it runs on every refresh)
 - Runs over all reports for all contacts and executes the configured function
 - Converts the result (guarding against bad ids) into minimally deleted files and writes them into PouchDB
 - Doesn't sync those deletes upwards
 - ~Initiates a compaction if anything was purged~ Does nothing because we auto-compact

I have tested it and it seems to nominally work.

Still to do:
 - Write tests!
 - Actually pull config from config
 - Document that config's existence, write a TL / CHT guide on how to use the feature
 - Performance test to make sure running like this on startup doesn't destroy a typically full phone in an obviously bad way. If it does, consider pausing between sets for n seconds to reduce constant cpu usage
 - Consider exposing this on the about page so users can manually run purge.
 - Consider putting this behind a "persisted queue", so if a user gets halfway through and refreshes we pick up where we left off.
 - Consider view warming. Doesn't really seem worth it on PouchDB, idk. Which would you pick etc.

More notes:
 - If at some point we want purge rules to only apply to certain people we could allow for the function to return a map of id to role, e.g. `['id1', 'id2']` -> `{id1: true, id2: ['role1', 'role2']}`
 - If we decide that we don't want to ship without it running on the server, while it was good practice for thinking about the problem and not much time investment I'd probably have to throw the vast majority of it away.

Interested in your thoughts.

medic/medic-webapp#5048

title: PouchDB replication _bulk_get requests no longer batched
body:
Since the upgrade to PouchDB `7.0.0` (in 3.1.0), replication `_bulk_get` requests are no longer batched (in standard PouchDB 100 docs limit). 
This is caused by [this commit](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/commit/2987c56311ae2d170d7c1d856470894f760a819a), which changes the moment `onChange` events are emitted.
Instead of being emitted sequentially, thus allowing the replicator to split the changes into batches, all `onChange` events are emitted at once and their processing delayed until `nextTick`. 
Together with the fact that our filtered replication ignores PouchDB limit of 100 changes per request, means that, for initial replication at least, there will be a single `_bulk_get` request to get all docs (potentially thousands). 

Do you think this could be a problem, @garethbowen? I'm afraid of timeouts specifically.

title: CouchDB 2.3.0 has reduced the allowed length of GET requests
body:
When making a view request PouchDB switches to use a POST if the URL with parameters exceeds [2000 characters](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/fb2ab0afe57a51da574ee3fac0bf1bd59fdbe502/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-abstract-mapreduce/src/index.js#L262). Against CouchDB 2.2.0 GET requests this long work as expected, but in CouchDB 2.3.0 they fail at around 1370 characters.

1. Raise an issue with CouchDB to change the limit back or at least document the change.
2. Raise an issue with PouchDB to change their limit - ideally submit a PR.
3. Patch our PouchDB in webapp, api, and sentinel to have a lower limit to be removed once it's fixed properly either by Couch or Pouch.

Thanks @dianabarsan for finding this!

title: Lazy loading visit information on the contacts LHS
body:
In UHC mode, render the contacts list on the LHS with a spinner waiting for the last visited and visit count information to be rendered. Leave enough white space that this information will render without moving any elements around.

![loading mock up](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2064938/49708894-81562300-fc96-11e8-8967-2ecfc429bb1a.PNG)

If the user filters or sorts by the last visited information then multiple stage render will be chaotic - render everything in one stage for these cases.

title: Lazy loading contact RHS sections
body:
Don't block rendering the page waiting for all the content, instead each section will load with a spinner with the content being rendered when ready. 

The shifting of content within the page from spinners is concerning, but we discussed two mitigations which can be investigated:

1. when the UI shifts, attempt to adjust the scroll position to minimize the disturbance, or if that isn't possible.
2. ignore any user touch for 1 second after shifting of content above the current scroll position.

Information in the contact summary which requires reports to be loaded should be moved into condition cards.

This is "Option 2c: Loading spinners" from [this design deck](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1TThN7MkhEB12np2x3o7evJRz0Gqb3E69Zll68pb8X-I/edit#slide=id.g498531a5d1_0_424).

title: 5082 - Make content-security-policy more strict
body:
# Description

I believe this is our most tightly constrained CSP without breaking anything. It requires a few "unsafe" configurations:

1. `imgSrc: data:` - "developers SHOULD NOT include either 'unsafe-inline', or data: as valid sources in their policies. Both enable XSS attacks by allowing code to be included directly in the document itself; they are best avoided completely." https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/#csp-directives
1. `scriptSrc: unsafe-eval` - We use `eval()` about 88 times and use `new Function()` about 17 times in inbox.js. "AngularJS makes use of this in the $parse service to provide a 30% increase in the speed of evaluating AngularJS expressions." https://docs.angularjs.org/api/ng/directive/ngCsp
1. `styleSrc: unsafe-inline` - Our dependency, `angular-ui-bootstrap` injects about 8 inline style blocks. Here is an example issue where they fix one of them https://github.com/angular-ui/bootstrap/issues/5470. The risks from unsafe css are reduced by fully constraining imgSrc (not done here) and by avoiding unsafe-eval (not done here).

#5082 

## Questions for Reviewer

1. I'm explicitly allowing the inline script for telemetry `window.startupTimes` - through a whitelisted hash. Another option would be to move that script into its own file and appcache it. As-is, if the content of this script ever changes, the corresponding hash will need to be updated. If we keep it as a hash, I'm unsure of the best method to keep the hash and script in sync (new test, calculate the hash in api, just pray, etc.). 
1. We may want to whitelist a hash for each of the eight style blocks from angular-ui-bootstrap instead of using`unsafe-inline` - I didn't do it because I'm not sure they are always the same for all browsers but they probably are and can follow-up if we close on that direction.

## Additional considerations

This change also makes the header larger. Including it on all resources (js, css, application/json, etc.) isn't required so one minor performance tweak we might consider here is setting it for `Accept: html` requests only. 

CSP also supports `report-uri` which can alert us when the security policy is violated (due to bugs or successful attacks). Might be worth opening an issue to enable this down the road.

## Testing

I went through some basic workflows in webapp + tried each actions in admin pages. In general though, this has risks of breaking edge-case functionalities or workflows I don't know about. Best to AT across all browsers as there are apparently some differences.

# Review checklist

- [ ] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/development/style-guide.md), documented if necessary.

With the API service spending too much time in migrations. This happens because the performance of the `extract_user_settings` migration degrades with each document in the _users document.  Tests were failing for me with ~300 docs in _users.

Running the E2E test suite creates documents in the _users database which are not always properly cleaned up. Normal development tasks may require many documents to be created in the _users database.

Tasks:
* Improve the logging in the E2E tests to include something like "If API is stuck in migrations, try cleaning up your _users database"
* It could also tell you where the logs are to check where it got up to
* It could probably even tell you whether it was API or Sentinel that got stuck

title: Don't write deploy_info if undefined
body:
# Description

When doing a non-Horticulturalist deploy, `medic` ddoc lacks the `deploy_info` property which horti adds. 
As a result, ddoc extraction would update `medic-client` every time it ran (because `undefined` properties don't get saved in CouchDB). 
Fix: only copy `deploy_info` if either old or new value exist. 

This would not occur in production deployments which are handled by Horticulturalist. 

medic/medic-webapp#5109

# Review checklist

- [ ] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/development/style-guide.md), documented if necessary.

title: Clean up the horti staging database
body:
The horti staging db ( https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org ) stores all our published artefacts so they can later be installed. Currently all tags (released versions) and branches (features in development) get published there and stored indefinitely. Once a branch gets merged/released there's no need to keep the build artefact around any more. Currently it's using 35GB which costs money and clogs up the horti UI with old branches.

Find a way to purge (or delete if purging isn't available) old feature branches. The simplest way is simply to delete them 3 months after the latest release. Be very careful not to delete tag releases.

If purging works then also update the `scripts/travis/cleanup.js` to purge instead of deleting the testing releases.

title: User cannot logout while offline
body:
If the user is offline and selects "Log out", they get to an error page and when they reconnect they are online.

**Steps to reproduce**:

1. Launch the app
1. Login
1. Go offline
1. Click "Log out" and confirm "yes"
1. Land on app's error page
1. Reconnect to data and click "retry"

**What should happen**:
User should be logged out

**What actually happens**:
User is still logged in

Possible data security implications of not being able to logout and hide your data.
Currently the session cookie is HttpOnly so it can't be deleted in script.

title: Only send tombstone deletes when document is still deleted
body:
If a document is deleted and then re-added (once or repeated), the deletes should not be included in the offline changes feed - even if the deleted `rev` is lower, PouchDB replication still considers the last rev it has received as winning. 

Discovered after fixing https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/5078 (send form deletes to offline users). 
When updating forms, medic-conf first deletes existent forms and then uploads new ones.

title: #4713 - Replace appcache with a service worker cache
body:
# Description 
This change replaces the underlying technology which allows the webapp to load while offline. This change removes the use of the legacy appcache and adds offline support via a PWA service worker. 
#4713

# Method
## Chrome 53 Constraint 
The technical approach taken in this proposed change is guided by a non-obvious constraint of service works in Chrome 53. Prior to Chrome 66, the web requests from the service worker don't include credentials (cookies, basic auth, etc). This means all resource we wish to cache must be accessible via unauthenticated endpoints. 

## Overview of my Approach

* **Service Worker Code** - I use the [swPrecache library from Google](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/sw-precache#service-worker-precache) to generate the service worker script at build time. SwPrecache has been replaced by [Workbox](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/workbox/) which is Google's latest solution for generating service workers. Details as to why I'm using the legacy technology discussed in "swPrecache vs Workbox" below.  
* **New public endpoints** - When API starts, I extract all cacheable resources from _design/medic and write them to a new directory in `api/src/extracted`. So instead of serving resources through the authenticated endpoint `/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js`, the same resource is served from the public `/js/inbox.js`. 
* **Initial service worker installation** - I updated bootstrapper to handle the synchronous install of the service worker and show an error + reload action if precaching of any resource fails. (#3568) 
* **Triggering Updates** - A service worker update should be triggered when any resource in the cache changes (if not, you have to refresh twice to get a change). Since the `service-worker.js` generated at build time contains a hash of every cached resource, watching the script itself for changes is sufficient to detect when a cache update is necessary.  I re-use "ddoc extract" pattern to trigger the updates. 
* **Updating** - When the service worker updates, only the files which have changed are downloaded. If the service worker fails to download a required file for any reason (eg. connectivity), I retry on a timer every five minutes until it is successful. Only after the service worker updates is the user prompted to refresh. 
* **Scope** - A service worker can't have a "scope" broader than its own location. So although I serve the javascript from `/js/service-worker.js`, I create an alias at `/service-worker.js` to give it broad control to handle all caching concerns. 
* **Upgrading from AppCache to Service Workers** - If you login to current master (where resources are cached via appcache) and upgrade to this change - it is important to clear the old cache before caching anew. It is not possible to clear the appcache programmatically. I set `<html manifest="empty">` which requests an empty manifest and clears the cache. 
* **Rewire** - I've added a dependency on the rewire library for mocha testing. It's awesome and we should use it! 
 
## swPrecache vs Workbox 
It is worth checking out the [Support Details for swPrecache](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/sw-precache#support). TLDR: "We would recommend Workbox for new projects" but "we’ll continue to support sw-precache". 
 
Workbox looks awesome. Most notably check out [enabling offline Google Analytics](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/workbox/modules/workbox-google-analytics). So why isn't this PR using Workbox? The short answer is we probably should – but this is a big PR and Workbox is going to complicate things.  
 
Here is why I'm using the swPrecache library: 
 
1. **The community support isn't perfect for either option** - Workbox 3 supports Chrome >51, but modern [Workbox 4 only supports Chrome >56](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/workbox/releases) so really both swPrecache and latests Workbox are [both not supporting us](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bVwh8PW6r88). 
1. **Partial Precache State** - SwPrecache is pretty much exactly what we want by default: it fails to install the service worker if any resource doesn't get precached and thus the possibility of a partial precached state. Workbox delivers a best effort precache and it isn't immediately obvious to me how to best avoid a partial precache state. 
1. **Dependent Scripts** - SwPrecache inlines all dependencies directly in the service worker so we just serve one script and we are done. Workbox has a modular build which deploys dependencies along-side your service worker (~20 files). A bit messy and not a perfect fit for our build script which ends up adding twenty more attachments to the database. A quick attempt to build only the required resources ended up with some dependencies being pulled from a cdn – which is problematic for projects using domain-based data contracts.  
 
All solvable problems, but a bit of untangling to do. Imo -- the best case would be using Workbox to output a script which does exactly what swPrecache is outputting now. I'm confident we can get there if we are interested in other features of Workbox *cough* - offline google analytics - *cough*. 
 
# Questions for Reviewer 

1. Let's discuss the general approach in this PR and maybe somebody can test a few scenarios on a device or two? If we like the result, maybe it is easier to carve this into chunks and review and submit in pieces. 
1. I just copied the list of resources to cache from appcache.manifest. We cache 29 files (some things which we maybe don't use). Maybe worth following up with an item to reduce how much we cache? 
1. The Application tab in devtools reports the disk use of appcache as 20.6MB and the same resources cached using service workers as 39.7MB. Unsure of the reason, but possible discussion point. 
1. It would be nice to get some guidance on exactly what horti scenarios would be good to test for this. 
1. Should we use the service worker to cache the favicon? 
1. Should we use the service worker to cache the login page? Even if you can't login, it's a better experience than seeing the non-localized white unbranded error page for login when offline. 
1. Upgrading from master to this change doesn't give the user the "Update" prompt because there is no change to a document being watched in master. Since this change won't be deployed atomically and will be instead packaged with other changes in v3.5 - I think that is safe. But we can consider tombstoning the legacy `appcache` document to make this change prompt an upgrade and also keep the database a bit cleaner. Looking for advice as I'm unsure how to best handle that. 
1. For performance reasons, we could consider making the service worker download and precache resources on the login page instead of after login. It is a one-line change which could benefit some users but possibly annoy others. 
1. Instead of using "ddoc-extraction," I considered calculating the hash of the service worker file at build-time and setting a single attribute on the medic-client ddoc. Think this would be cleaner? 
1. I put the core grunt logic into its own file instead of dumping it into the Gruntfile.js. I find that Gruntfile really hard to parse, and easily get lost in its large indentations. What do you think of starting to chop up that file into separate more manageable pieces (as done here)? 
1. Want to add a new UI state into the bootstrapper which says something like "Downloading App..." For the duration of the period in which we precache the service worker's resources? 
1. This change will block testing on insecure origins except localhost. This is pretty awkward for testing dev builds on a phone – I ran a DNS server + nginx proxy + vpn on my phone to work around it. This is likely something we should address in this change or shortly after. Looking to discuss the best approach. 
1. Is it safe the remove the write access controls to the deprecated appcache document in this change? 

# Scenarios I Tested

1. Incognito, login. Go offline. Refresh: user should get offline experience. 
1. Incognito, delete a required attachment, login: user should see an error dialog prompting to check connection. Rebuild and click retry: login should succeed and page should work offline. 
1. Incognito, login, update a css file, build, sync: user should see prompt to update. Update: user should see change in css appear. Network shows only the css file being updated. 
1. Incognito, login, update a css file, build, delete the css attachment in db, sync: user should see error in console and should not be prompted to update. Rebuild: after five minutes user should see prompt to update. Update: user should see change in css appear. 
1. If service-worker.js results in 404, then the app should not load and user should see error prompting to check connection. 
1. Incognito, login, update a css file, build, refresh without syncing: user should see prompt to update after refresh. Update: user should see change in css appear. 
1. Incognito, login to master (AppCache version). Rebuild to proposed change, sync. User should see prompt to update.

title: Support binding to fields.patient_uuid
body:
In some configurations the patient_id field holds the patient shortcode,
while the patient_uuid field holds the internal id.

For tasks and targets it's important that we know how to bind to the
UUID as well, because otherwise users may see bugs while offline. For
example, a task wouldn't close until the report that closes the task is
synced upwards, run through by Sentinel, and synced back down.

Less important for purging, but it's better that we keep the function
logic the same.

title: 4713 - Replace appcache with a service worker cache
body:
# Description 
This change replaces the underlying technology which allows the webapp to load while offline. This change removes the use of the legacy appcache and adds offline support via a PWA service worker. 
#4713

# Method
## Chrome 53 Constraint 
The technical approach taken in this proposed change is guided by a non-obvious constraint of service works in Chrome 53. Prior to Chrome 66, the web requests from the service worker don't include credentials (cookies, basic auth, etc). This means all resource we wish to cache must be accessible via unauthenticated endpoints. 

## Overview of my Approach

* **Service Worker Code** - I use the [swPrecache library from Google](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/sw-precache#service-worker-precache) to generate the service worker script at build time. SwPrecache has been replaced by [Workbox](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/workbox/) which is Google's latest solution for generating service workers. Details as to why I'm using the legacy technology discussed in "swPrecache vs Workbox" below.  
* **New public endpoints** - When API starts, I extract all cacheable resources from _design/medic and write them to a new directory in `api/src/extracted`. So instead of serving resources through the authenticated endpoint `/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js`, the same resource is served from the public `/js/inbox.js`. 
* **Initial service worker installation** - I updated bootstrapper to handle the synchronous install of the service worker and show an error + reload action if precaching of any resource fails. (#3568) 
* **Triggering Updates** - A service worker update should be triggered when any resource in the cache changes (if not, you have to refresh twice to get a change). Since the `service-worker.js` generated at build time contains a hash of every cached resource, watching the script itself for changes is sufficient to detect when a cache update is necessary.  I re-use "ddoc extract" pattern to trigger the updates. 
* **Updating** - When the service worker updates, only the files which have changed are downloaded. If the service worker fails to download a required file for any reason (eg. connectivity), I retry on a timer every five minutes until it is successful. Only after the service worker updates is the user prompted to refresh. 
* **Scope** - A service worker can't have a "scope" broader than its own location. So although I serve the javascript from `/js/service-worker.js`, I create an alias at `/service-worker.js` to give it broad control to handle all caching concerns. 
* **Upgrading from AppCache to Service Workers** - If you login to current master (where resources are cached via appcache) and upgrade to this change - it is important to clear the old cache before caching anew. It is not possible to clear the appcache programmatically. I set `<html manifest="empty">` which requests an empty manifest and clears the cache. 
* **Rewire** - I've added a dependency on the rewire library for mocha testing. It's awesome and we should use it! 
 
## swPrecache vs Workbox 
It is worth checking out the [Support Details for swPrecache](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/sw-precache#support). TLDR: "We would recommend Workbox for new projects" but "we’ll continue to support sw-precache". 
 
Workbox looks awesome. Most notably check out [enabling offline Google Analytics](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/workbox/modules/workbox-google-analytics). So why isn't this PR using Workbox? The short answer is we probably should – but this is a big PR and Workbox is going to complicate things.  
 
Here is why I'm using the swPrecache library: 
 
1. **The community support isn't perfect for either option** - Workbox 3 supports Chrome >51, but modern [Workbox 4 only supports Chrome >56](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/workbox/releases) so really both swPrecache and latests Workbox are [both not supporting us](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bVwh8PW6r88). 
1. **Partial Precache State** - SwPrecache is pretty much exactly what we want by default: it fails to install the service worker if any resource doesn't get precached and thus the possibility of a partial precached state. Workbox delivers a best effort precache and it isn't immediately obvious to me how to best avoid a partial precache state. 
1. **Dependent Scripts** - SwPrecache inlines all dependencies directly in the service worker so we just serve one script and we are done. Workbox has a modular build which deploys dependencies along-side your service worker (~20 files). A bit messy and not a perfect fit for our build script which ends up adding twenty more attachments to the database. A quick attempt to build only the required resources ended up with some dependencies being pulled from a cdn – which is problematic for projects using domain-based data contracts.  
 
All solvable problems, but a bit of untangling to do. Imo -- the best case would be using Workbox to output a script which does exactly what swPrecache is outputting now. I'm confident we can get there if we are interested in other features of Workbox *cough* - offline google analytics - *cough*. 
 
# Questions for Reviewer 

1. Let's discuss the general approach in this PR and maybe somebody can test a few scenarios on a device or two? If we like the result, maybe it is easier to carve this into chunks and review and submit in pieces. 
1. I just copied the list of resources to cache from appcache.manifest. We cache 29 files (some things which we maybe don't use). Maybe worth following up with an item to reduce how much we cache? 
1. The Application tab in devtools reports the disk use of appcache as 20.6MB and the same resources cached using service workers as 39.7MB. Unsure of the reason, but possible discussion point. 
1. It would be nice to get some guidance on exactly what horti scenarios would be good to test for this. 
1. Should we use the service worker to cache the favicon? 
1. Should we use the service worker to cache the login page? Even if you can't login, it's a better experience than seeing the non-localized white unbranded error page for login when offline. 
1. Upgrading from master to this change doesn't give the user the "Update" prompt because there is no change to a document being watched in master. Since this change won't be deployed atomically and will be instead packaged with other changes in v3.5 - I think that is safe. But we can consider tombstoning the legacy `appcache` document to make this change prompt an upgrade and also keep the database a bit cleaner. Looking for advice as I'm unsure how to best handle that. 
1. For performance reasons, we could consider making the service worker download and precache resources on the login page instead of after login. It is a one-line change which could benefit some users but possibly annoy others. 
1. Instead of using "ddoc-extraction," I considered calculating the hash of the service worker file at build-time and setting a single attribute on the medic-client ddoc. Think this would be cleaner? 
1. I put the core grunt logic into its own file instead of dumping it into the Gruntfile.js. I find that Gruntfile really hard to parse, and easily get lost in its large indentations. What do you think of starting to chop up that file into separate more manageable pieces (as done here)? 
1. Want to add a new UI state into the bootstrapper which says something like "Downloading App..." For the duration of the period in which we precache the service worker's resources? 
1. This change will block testing on insecure origins except localhost. This is pretty awkward for testing dev builds on a phone – I ran a DNS server + nginx proxy + vpn on my phone to work around it. This is likely something we should address in this change or shortly after. Looking to discuss the best approach. 
1. Is it safe the remove the write access controls to the deprecated appcache document in this change? 

# Scenarios I Tested

1. Incognito, login. Go offline. Refresh: user should get offline experience. 
1. Incognito, delete a required attachment, login: user should see an error dialog prompting to check connection. Rebuild and click retry: login should succeed and page should work offline. 
1. Incognito, login, update a css file, build, sync: user should see prompt to update. Update: user should see change in css appear. Network shows only the css file being updated. 
1. Incognito, login, update a css file, build, delete the css attachment in db, sync: user should see error in console and should not be prompted to update. Rebuild: after five minutes user should see prompt to update. Update: user should see change in css appear. 
1. If service-worker.js results in 404, then the app should not load and user should see error prompting to check connection. 
1. Incognito, login, update a css file, build, refresh without syncing: user should see prompt to update after refresh. Update: user should see change in css appear. 
1. Incognito, login to master (AppCache version). Rebuild to proposed change, sync. User should see prompt to update. 

# License
The software is provided under AGPL-3.0. Contributions to this project are accepted under the same license.

title: 5082 - Make content-security-policy more strict
body:
# Description

I believe this is our most tightly constrained CSP without breaking anything. It requires a few "unsafe" configurations:

1. `imgSrc: data:` - "developers SHOULD NOT include either 'unsafe-inline', or data: as valid sources in their policies. Both enable XSS attacks by allowing code to be included directly in the document itself; they are best avoided completely." https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/#csp-directives
1. `scriptSrc: unsafe-eval` - We use `eval()` about 88 times and use `new Function()` about 17 times in inbox.js. "AngularJS makes use of this in the $parse service to provide a 30% increase in the speed of evaluating AngularJS expressions." https://docs.angularjs.org/api/ng/directive/ngCsp
1. `styleSrc: unsafe-inline` - Our dependency, `angular-ui-bootstrap` injects about 8 inline style blocks. Here is an example issue where they fix one of them https://github.com/angular-ui/bootstrap/issues/5470. The risks from unsafe css are reduced by fully constraining imgSrc (not done here) and by avoiding unsafe-eval (not done here).

#5082 

## Questions for Reviewer

1. I'm explicitly allowing the inline script for telemetry `window.startupTimes` - through a whitelisted hash. Another option would be to move that script into its own file and appcache it. As-is, if the content of this script ever changes, the corresponding hash will need to be updated. If we keep it as a hash, I'm unsure of the best method to keep the hash and script in sync (new test, calculate the hash in api, just pray, etc.). 
1. We may want to whitelist a hash for each of the eight style blocks from angular-ui-bootstrap instead of using`unsafe-inline` - I didn't do it because I'm not sure they are always the same for all browsers but they probably are and can follow-up if we close on that direction.

## Additional considerations

This change also makes the header larger. Including it on all resources (js, css, application/json, etc.) isn't required so one minor performance tweak we might consider here is setting it for `Accept: html` requests only. 

CSP also supports `report-uri` which can alert us when the security policy is violated (due to bugs or successful attacks). Might be worth opening an issue to enable this down the road.

## Testing

I went through some basic workflows in webapp + tried each actions in admin pages. In general though, this has risks of breaking edge-case functionalities or workflows I don't know about. Best to AT across all browsers as there are apparently some differences.

# Review checklist

title: Outgoing messages columns should not wrap on smaller screens
body:
Currently, when the screen size is decreased, the columns on the outgoing messages page wrap so that they are underneath earlier columns. This makes for very poor usability and makes the page nearly unusable. 

The App Settings console is meant to only work on desktop screens, but it needs to at least be somewhat responsive, so that those working on smaller laptops can still use it. Recommended approach: Never wrap columns! In the case of the 15 in laptop screenshot below, we should probably just be further reducing the width of the middle "Message" column to allow room for the "Last update" column in its proper place on the right. If the screen really gets too small, the columns should stay where they are, but just fall outside the viewable area, and the viewer can scroll left and right to view everything.

Here's what it looks like on my 15 in laptop at full size. The "Last update" column is wrapping to appear underneath the "Recipient" column.
![messages-wrapping1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/50918555-6097ff00-13f5-11e9-91d4-ca8d2aae0068.jpg)

The problems get even worse when you go even smaller. Here, you can see that three columns, "Status", "Due", and "Last update" and their data are now all appearing below the first three columns.
![messages-wrapping2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/50918830-20854c00-13f6-11e9-86b4-4fc1f003968a.jpg)

title: Clarify and streamline process for investigating e2e flakey test failures
body:
There were four issues related to flakey e2e tests in v3.4. Investigating these failures is something devs spend time doing and we can be more productive as a team by improving how our e2e tests run and how failures are reported.

A few potential improvements to look at:

* Can we have an easy flag or command which which runs e2e tests in chrome instead of headless to tests are visible?
* Travis uploads some log files to s3. Several devs (myself included) don't know what is getting uploaded or how to access the files.
* Can we get a screenshot at the time of the flakey test failure?
* Can we see the chrome console at the time of the failure?
* Can we see a full dump of the DOM at the time of the failure?
* Bonus points if e2e tests fail because of errors in the console logs during the test.
* There are some tips/tricks for investigating e2e test failures (like enabling protractor's control flow and [this](https://github.com/gabduss/runProtractorVsCodeExtension) vscode extension). A quick doc capturing these tips might be helpful. Maybe a new section in [this](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/development/testing.md) or alike.

title: Guard against bad HTTP codes in error reporting
Interrupted replication fails because of `seq_interval` changes parameter
body:
CouchDB 2.0 introduced an optimization on the _changes endpoint, used by sending the `seq_interval` request parameter. 

>seq_interval (number) – When fetching changes in a batch, setting the seq_interval parameter tells CouchDB to only calculate the update seq with every Nth result returned. By setting seq_interval=<batch size> , where <batch size> is the number of results requested per batch, load can be reduced on the source CouchDB database; computing the seq value across many shards (esp. in highly-sharded databases) is expensive in a heavily loaded CouchDB cluster.

PouchDB 6.4.x has been using `seq_interval` in all replication requests and I, mistakenly, forward this parameter to the upstream `_changes` request when doing filtered replication. 

PouchDB 6.4.x batches the `_bulk_get` requests when replicating (standard batch size is 100) - so every 100 changes it will write a remote checkpointer doc. The Checkpointer doc stores the last replicated seq. When writing this checkpointer, PouchDB decides that this seq is either the seq of the last change in the batch it has just processed OR the `last_seq` received from the _changes request. 

CouchDB _changes requests with `_doc_ids` filter, `seq_interval` and `limit` (these parameters are used in our upstream changes requests) don't populate seq-s in the expected positions: every n changes from head to tail, instead every n changes from tail to head.  (If the limit parameter is removed, the seq-s are positioned correctly - unfortunately we cannot remove the limit parameter as PouchDB library forcefully tries to batch changes requests). 

This issue has been fixed in PouchDB 7.0.0 (https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/issues/6809) , 
but we are still affected by this.
Affected versions are: 3.0 and upgrades from 2.x -> 3.x (devices running Pouch 6.4.x replicating from Medic API 3.x).

title: Pass user context to the purge function
body:
In conversations about facility-based workflows we are seeing that the purge function needed by a CHW could be different than that needed by their supervisors or facility-based users. We are seeing this requirement for closed-loop referrals where facility staff are using the mobile app in offline mode to have tasks about their patients, but only need very specific reports to do their work. If they have all the reports for all their patients they would have too many docs on their device for it to function properly. As a result, we should make sure to pass the user's context information (ie lineage, role) to the purge function so that we can purge based on that context information.

_This is a follow up to #5048, and came up via discussion about partner requirements with @SCdF_

title: Node domains causing a memory leak
body:
[Domains in Node](https://nodejs.org/api/domain.html) are deprecated because they're bad. In particular, we call Domain.dispose which has been removed in Node v10 so uncaught exceptions cause even more exceptions to be thrown.

Domains can be used to limit errors to one specific request, but currently we're exiting the process which clearly isn't limiting it at all. Replace the use of domains with an unhandled exception handler.

title: Downgrade PouchDB to 6.x
body:
As of version 7.0.0 PouchDB no longer batches `_all_docs` and `_bulk_get` requests during replication (see related issue https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/5076 for detailed explanation and alternative solution), instead executes these requests attempting to get all docs it has received from _changes in one single batch. 

That has proven to make it impossible to replicate large users (10k+ docs), with these users either failing replication at the first `_all_docs` request or at the next `_bulk_get` request. On top of that, PouchDB has a fallback replication algorithm for cases when it's replicating from a 1.x Couch that does not implement `_bulk_get` endpoint, which is to request every document individually via `GET`. This causes Pouch to launch a very large number of GET requests concurrently, that trigger `ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` errors (maybe crashing the app on the phone? This is TBD). 

The quickest fix is to downgrade PouchDB used in Webapp to 6.4.3 (the version used in 3.0 and before).

title: Offline users are caching unused font files
body:
Our current proposed service worker caches about 2.5MB of font files. Here is the current list of files and their sizes: 

Filename | Size (kB) 
-- | -- 
enketo-icons-v2.eot | 5 
enketo-icons-v2.svg | 10 
enketo-icons-v2.ttf | 5 
enketo-icons-v2.woff | 4  
FontAwesome.otf | 135  
fontawesome-webfont.eot | 166 
fontawesome-webfont.svg | 445 
fontawesome-webfont.ttf | 166 
fontawesome-webfont.woff | 99 
fontawesome-webfont.woff2 | 78 
NotoSans-BoldItalic.ttf | 291 
NotoSans-Bold.ttf | 416 
NotoSans-Italic.ttf | 280 
NotoSans-Regular.ttf | 415 

Summary of the font formats and the browsers/users they are intended for: https://transfonter.org/formats 

## Font Awesome (985kb) 

907kB potential savings -- the Webapp and modern browsers all use the `woff2` format (78 kb). Other formats are required by alternative browsers but I suspect there are insufficient offline users on these browsers to warrant precaching the resources (offline users outside of app and outside of chrome). With the service workers, it is pretty easy to use an alternative caching strategy so they are cached if/when used. 

## NotoSans (1402kb) 

571kB potential savings -- We don't use the Italic or BoldItalic versions. So these seem unnecessary to precache. We can consider to not precache them and make a unit test which confirms we never use `font-style: italic;` and if the test fails, it will remind the dev to just add them back into the cache. 

Follow-up after #5219

title: Message queue not loading when translations are missing
body:
When loading Admin's message queue, we try to load all languages in Angular before generating messages. We do that by iterating over all languages and issuing a call to Angular Translate, which effectively loads the language. 
If the key we are trying to translate doesn't exist, Angular Translate throws an error and, as a result, the message queue does not load. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/51597103-1f2e4600-1f03-11e9-9132-ceb530911e31.png)

Discovered after translations failed to be updated by an upgrade (https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/5271).

title: Updates seq of live changes in batched changes feeds
body:
# Description

PouchDB (as of 7.0.0) has four mechanisms for handling `last_seq` while replicating:

1. In the [Changes handler](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/1da0eb6fbe33ea1aeb55e2b16f479a992ebcb5be/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-adapter-http/src/index.js#L1026) it uses `result.last_seq` to batch changes; this affected us in API prior to batching and Couch 2.3
2. In the Replication Handler ([here](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/1da0eb6fbe33ea1aeb55e2b16f479a992ebcb5be/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-replication/src/replicate.js#L308) and [here](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/1da0eb6fbe33ea1aeb55e2b16f479a992ebcb5be/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-replication/src/replicate.js#L133)) it uses the `seq` of the last change in a batch OR `result.last_seq` when writing local and remote checkpointer
3. In the Replication Handler ([here](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/1da0eb6fbe33ea1aeb55e2b16f479a992ebcb5be/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-replication/src/replicate.js#L326)) it uses the `seq` of the last change in the whole response to use as a `since` param in the next _changes request
4. In the Replication Handler ([here](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/1da0eb6fbe33ea1aeb55e2b16f479a992ebcb5be/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-replication/src/replicate.js#L344)) it uses the `result.last_seq` when writing the last checkpoint when replication is completed (no results returned by last _changes request). 

The issue this PR is fixing is when we receive changes, in between our view calls and the time that our upstream _changes request resolves, which should be seen by our user; these changes are pushed to our current response, because they would be skipped if our upstream result advances the checkpointer seq beyond theirs. 

There is no way of reliably comparing seq's or even knowing how many more changes we have left (the `pending` param is not affected by our _doc_ids filter), so I've decided to push these changes to any request, the downside being that they could end up being processed by PouchDB twice. 
In order to not have their possibly more recent `seq`s alter the replication algorithm in Pouch, before appending them to the result, I'm updating their seq to be equal to the `last_seq` received by the upstream filtered request. 

Also fixes a race condition where a new doc would be added before upstream changes feed responds, but the live changes feed receives it AFTER we send a response. Discovered because an e2e test failed a couple of times. 

medic/medic-webapp#5076

The [export data controller](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/api/src/controllers/export-data.js#L126) uses node domains to catch all errors and handle them. This is deprecated and can cause memory leaks (although I don't think this particular code leaks).

Switch to managing the errors without using domains.

@garethbowen what do you know about this flag, and what it means? What situations did this flag fix for you?

title: Spelling.
4750 Add redux with first store element
body:
# Description

The initial approach here was supposed to be to move controllers/templates over to components one at a time. After many hours attempting to turn `ContactsEdit` into a component (which you can see in the second commit if you're curious), it became clear this wasn't a good idea as migrated components would be reading from and updating the redux store, while unmigrated controllers/templates would be reading from and updating `$scope`, so there'd be two sources of truth. Also, migrating just one component to have an isolate scope required a huge amount of properties and functions to be migrated across to the redux way in one go, quite possibly breaking things.

Instead it seems to make more sense to make this migration by taking properties one at a time out of `$scope` and moving them to the redux store, updating all app references to this property at once. This means that technically nothing will be a "component" in name until the entire app state has been moved over to redux, but they will be slowly becoming components in spirit (that is, they'll slowly start to use the redux store, and thus effectively work in isolate scope).

This PR starts with moving the `cancelCallback` property from `$scope` to redux, and updates all app references. The function names were renamed from `setTarget` and `clearTarget` as it seems less confusing to have everything using the one name.

medic/medic#4750

**Steps to reproduce**:

title: Reminders are not working
body:
Reminders are not sent because the `clinic` docs  are not hydrated before passing them to generate the message, thus the recipient phone number will never be matched: all reminder tasks will have a recipient of `"clinic"`. At least, if the message configuration is not templated to be unique, the tasks will get a `duplicate` state and not spam gateway. 

Also:

- back in 2013 someone renamed a task field from `code` to `form` (https://github.com/medic/medic/commit/e626ba7acba951a139a6d176eec634e0cea0f448#diff-664792df5ba92ac7b86ac6a683087fdeL98) but the view which checks when last reminders were created still checks for `code`, so it's a useless view ATM https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/fc315d632da137105bf6563ae121f25007314f40/ddocs/medic/views/sent_reminders/map.js#L4

- reminders don't have a `timestamp` or `due` property - they have a `ts` property, so their position in admin message-queue will be dependent to `doc.reported_date` (in this case, the moment the clinic was created).

Looking into projects, there is only one project that has "reminders" configured. 

Is this a feature that we should fix or deprecate? 

cc @garethbowen @abbyad

title: Date formatting in exports is not human readable
body:
First raised in [this medic-projects issue](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/5790) the export files are formatting the date as millis since the epoch which isn't easy for end users to read. These files should be able to be read without having to apply further calculations.

Unfortunately changing the output format would break API compatibility for anyone scripting against the export endpoints.

Add a new parameter to the export endpoints for `human-readable` (or come up with a better name) which defaults to `false` for backwards compatibility. Then update the webapp to add the new parameter everywhere it's being called. Remember to update the API documentation as well.

title: Warn when replicating too many docs
body:
Users are trying to replicate more docs sometimes on purpose and sometimes due to misconfiguration. This leads to poor user experience and can impact other users by monopolising server resources. We need to do a better job of communicating the maximum number of recommended docs and also warning when users have been configured incorrectly.

1. @SCdF Has made a start on an API to return the number of docs a user will replicate - take [his PR](https://github.com/medic/medic/pull/5356) and get it production ready and and merged. Consider caching to reduce load.
2. When creating a user through medic-conf or the admin app query this API and warn (but don't block) the configurer if the doc count is too high.
3. When a user replication request is received log a warning in the API log if the doc count is too high. Consider how to not spam the logs, possibly batching the writes together so it's written once per hour.
4. When a user does an initial replication show a confirm dialog so they are aware that their doc count is unusually high.

The definition of "too high" is up for debate but I think we should warn at 10,000 docs for now. This can be raised when we improve scalability.

title: Message recipient defaults to sender when recipient is explicit
body:
This is how the recipient phone number is determined at the moment:
https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/acff94a24775080ffda5927570757c6c0ffe99b6/shared-libs/message-utils/src/index.js#L105

where 
- `phone` is valid if `recipient` is an expression (`clinic`, `reporting_unit`, `report.contact.phone` etc) that is valid against the context
- `from` is `report.from || (report.contact && report.contact.phone)`
- `recipient` is the explicit recipient (which could be an actual phone number)

If you'd want to generate a message that should be sent to a specific explicit phone number, you will only succeed if the generating report does not have a `from` or `contact.phone`.

**TLDR**
Transitions configured with explicit recipients and `multi_report_alerts` will not create messages with correct recipients.

**Steps to reproduce**:
- Pick a simple transition that can add a message with a specific recipient, for example: `conditional_alerts`. Example will continue with specific scenario configuring `conditional_alerts`.
- Enable the transition
- Add the following configuration (or similar):
```
"alerts": [{
  "form": "P",
  "condition": "true",
  "message": "this is my test message",
  "recipient": "+40755203040"
}]
```
(you will likely already have an `alerts` property in your settings, either replace or add as a new entry).
- Go to admin and submit a P form (from a different number that the one configured as your alert recipient, it can even be an unknown phone number!)
- Allow sentinel to process the report and check it

**What should happen**:
- The report should have a task with "this is my test message" message to be sent to "+40755203040"

**What actually happens**:
- The report has a task with "this is my test message" message to be sent to the sender phone number.


As an alternative scenario, and the way I discovered this error, you can use `multi_report_alerts` transition.
Add a configuration like:

```
 "multi_report_alerts": [{
  "name": "test",
  "is_report_counted": "function(r, l) { return true }",
  "num_reports_threshold": 2,
  "message": "multi_report_message",
  "recipients": ["new_report.from"],
  "time_window_in_days": 1,
  "forms": ["N"]
}],
```

Then submit 2 N forms from different phone numbers. 
What you would expect is that your second form should have 2 tasks with `multi_report_message` message and to be sent to the 2 numbers that you submitted N forms with.
Instead, both tasks are marked to be sent to the last submitter's phone, with one of the tasks marked with `duplicate` state.

This effectively breaks `multi_report_alerts` transition, as it parses the phones before generating messages and provides explicit phone numbers to `message-utils`, thus all messages will be sent to the last submitter's phone instead of the configured recipients.

title: RFC: An `_id` scheme for Medic 4.0
body:
**NB:** This is in the 4.0 "some day" project because it's obviously a huge change that would require nearly all documents to be rewritten and all offline users to re-replicate. We have quite a few of these ideas and are slowly collecting them together so we can try to only do this once.

This ticket exists to create discussion and provoke thought on how we could use this incredibly rare opportunity to be allowed to change our schema to our advantage.

# RFC: New `_id` scheme

This new `_id` scheme is an attempt to:
 - Increase data integrity by tying the location of a document to its identity, more fully expressing the complications around moving
 - Increase replication performance and decrease code complexity by allowing filtered replication based entirely around knowing a user's `facility_id` (available from their authentication record) and parsing ids in the changes feed, removing many other moving parts
 - Allow various simplifications based around being able to predict authorization / location based off id or id query ranges alone.
 - Increase native CouchDB performance by following CouchDB's proposed guidelines for id entropy

Currently we have four main different styles of identifier:
 - Static ids known at "compile" time, e.g. `_design/medic`, `settings`
 - Pseudo-static identifiers prepended with their type, e.g., `form:pregnancy`
 - Random uuids that are almost certainly a contact or a report
 - prepended random uuids (e.g. info documents) to provide meta information about the type above

The core idea is to replace the third and fourth item with a prepend-based concept similar but grander than the second type.

## A quick example

Here is an example of the `_id` of a CHW:

```
place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/contact/USLdS01USYCKGyFZSyDZUA==
```

Scary!

Here is a pregnancy report generated by.. actually we don't care who the author is. Generated *for* a mother, in a family, in the CHW's area / clinic:

```
place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/OBQeIGqaRbaAEjfccmLcMQ==/contact/VPch4hVNQoy5dRzds8hYUQ==/report/d12isV79RVmk112tlKxLRw==
```

SCARIER!

## Details

If it's not already obvious, the idea here is that ids are a descriptor for where and what something is, in a similar style to REST endpoint routes:

```
DH:     place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==
HC:     place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==
Clinic: place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==
CHW:    place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/contact/USLdS01USYCKGyFZSyDZUA==
Family: place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/OBQeIGqaRbaAEjfccmLcMQ==
Mother: place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/OBQeIGqaRbaAEjfccmLcMQ==/contact/VPch4hVNQoy5dRzds8hYUQ==
Preg:   place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/OBQeIGqaRbaAEjfccmLcMQ==/contact/VPch4hVNQoy5dRzds8hYUQ==/report/d12isV79RVmk112tlKxLRw==
```

**Note 1:** There is more or less information we could add here, and we need to carefully consider what will and will not be useful, looking forward to hopefully not having to change this format for years to come. For example, we are not encoding the form type in the report url here. Do we want to? I'm not sure!

**Note 2:** The component identifiers are still UUIDs, they are just base64 instead of base16 to compress them a little. Code to achieve this in Node can be seen in the appendix. Code to achieve this in a browser is slightly more of a pain, but certainly not unachievable.

## Features this unlocks

### Increased data integrity

We can trivially extend `validate_doc_update` to ensure that a record's internally expressed hierarchy matches their identifier. This is nice because its codifying a presumption we already work off, that a record's location is immutable.

Currently you can "move" a record by altering its internal hierarchy. This is in the scary land of "undefined behaviours". It will almost certainly not work 100% correctly, and may work unpredictably, giving you different answers between different parts of the code, and different releases (even those where changes like this are not expressed in the semver, such as a patch level refactor).

In this new scheme, if you wish to move a record you have to delete the original and create a new record, forcing it to be deleted off devices and added only to those devices it's allowed to be on, and to be guaranteed to be refered to consistently throughout the applications that reference it.

### Faster scalable replication

_(NB: I realise replication is a very complicated subject. I **think** this is right, but I acknowledge I may be missing something very obvious which either makes the implementation more complicated / less beneficial, or even a non-starter. The purpose of this ticket is to discuss that if it arises.)_

With this id scheme we should be able to perform filtered replication using only:
 - The user's `facility_id`, pulled from their user document
 - The raw `_changes` feed as asked for by the user's request, probably with some limit multiplier for efficiency

CHW execution flow:
 - A restricted user hits the `_changes` endpoint, with e.g. `GET _changes?since=200&limit=100` with no other parameters
 - We simultaneously request the user's facility_id (we may already have this depending on what authication has run) and proxy the `_changes` feed to Couch, possibly muliplying the `limit` by some multiplier (e.g. 2x, or the number of known restricted users) as we presume some filtering will occur
 - Once we get the `_changes` results back we walk through every change `id`, and delete it out of the changes result unless:
     + If it's part of a whitelist known at compile time, e.g. a collection of static ids (`settings`) and partial ids (`/^form:/`)
     + If it `startsWith` their facility id, and does not end in `/purged`
 - Once we've done this, if our change count is less than the provided limit we loop until we've filled our changes feed
 - The final changes feed contains the same outer metadata (such as `last_seq`) as the last changes feed in the loop, but with the filtered list of ids.

Supervisor flow is nearly identical, except that we split over `/` and use that to determine if the record is too "far away" from the supervisor's facility to be replicated, based on their configured replication depth.

This is all you need to do, and all the support structures you need.

This scheme doesn't need:
 - specific views
 - tombstone generation
 - users providing their known documents

It supports both deleted documents and server-side purging.

It should also be very fast, use very little memory, and be embarrassingly parallel, lending itself to being multi-threaded, either inside api/nodejs, or written in an entirely different language which is easier to thread safely.

### Simplicity through predictability

There are probably lots of ways we can use this id scheme to both remove existing views, as well as running mango queries off the base id index.

For example, it is likely we could replace initial replication with three queries:
 - bulk docs for known static files
 - ranged query for `form:` ids (reports)
 - ranged query based on the user's facility id (this one involves updating our auth scanning in api to remove purged documents)

Correct authentication for documents can now be done by looking at ids at all points, probably simplifying various types of auth. E.g., you can reject GET requests before performing them, as well as being able to detect invalid query ranges (against ids).

There are probably more things you can do here.

### Increase native CouchDB performance

CouchDB works best when record id entropy tends towards the end of the id, not the start or evenly spread. This is why when you ask CouchDB to generate ids sequential requests generate very similar identifiers.

Moving to this scheme will correct our entropy distribution to be more CouchDB-friendly, presumably increasing performance in various ways.

## Downsides of this approach

Apart from the obvious re-replicate everything again thing.

 - If we ever want to replicate based on something not in our resulting id scheme we either have to change all ids again, or change replication back, or have some kind of `/more` feature in ids where we know that we have to pull that document out and hand-inspect it to fulfil more rule requirements
 - Purging has to be global. An option to get around this (if it's truely needed) could be to prepend chunks after `/purge/` describing the depths at which this purge is relevant, e.g. the chunk describing the clinic for CHWs, and the chunk describing the HC for supervisors.

# Appendix

## UUID generation

```js
// This is Nodejs code. Browser code is left as an execise for the reader
const uuid = require('uuid');

const uuid64 = () => {
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(16); // Buffers are 8-bit, 16*8 => 128bits
    uuid(null, buffer)
    return buffer
        .toString('base64')
        .replace(/\//, '-');
}

uuid64();
```

## ID entropy

Presuming a good UUID implementation, a single UUID already has 2^128 bits of entropy, enough to never conflict. The `_id`s described above have absurd amounts of entropy, more than 2^768 depending how you calculate entropy and from whose perspective.

We could consider reducing this. For example, instead of generating an 128bit UUID per node, instead generate something smaller, say 32 bits. We would have to think carefully about how this works, because probability theory is confusing and we don't want to get it wrong.

## Migration

### Server side

The smart thing to do here would literally be to start again: we would write a script that loads all docs from the source db, renames them based on this scheme and writes them to the target db.

### Client side

Client-side migration being a pain is generic to the theoretical 4.0 release, and so ideas discussed here apply to the entire project.

As we're changing the replication scheme, one thing we could do is detect old versions by checking for old style replication requests and only returning a fake static changes feed containing the new code. Ideally we'd also be able to detect old-style upward replication and 404 / otherwise block it from occuring, either by something we're currently doing, or by adding a flag to >=4.0.0 upward replication and detecting the lack of that flag.

This should isolate the user's device in its current <4.0.0 bubble. They can use the app as normal with no disruptions, and will be updated once they restart.

Once they restart and 4.0.0 code is running we can do whatever we want. Specifically:
 - Complete a full, now-unblocked upward replication to make sure that everything left on their phone is pushed upward, using some kind of MitM to change the document identifier:
     + If we MitM client-side (fetch, service workers), change the `_id` to `_old/${_id}` and write a Sentinel transition would works out their real new id and re-writes their contents against the new id (on top of an existing doc or as a new one as needed)
     + If we MitM server-side (api) we don't need sentinel, we can do it in the api write
 - Delete the existing client-side PouchDB, and start a full initial replication from scratch.
 - Start as normal

title: Optimize the `fix-user-db-security` migration for databases with many users
body:
It currently doesn't do any batching, and generates N parallel PUT requests to CouchDB, where N === the user count.

This is almost certainly A Bad Idea™ for larger databases.

We should at least not make those PUTs all concurrent.

This should be backported to 3.2.x.

title: Errors when navigating away from edited forms
body:
We have a feature that shows a popup when navigating away from an edited form: https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/4013 . This is part of 3.3. This is not working as expected in latest code. 

**Steps to reproduce**:
- Open the app (user type is not relevant as long as you can open some sort of Enketo form). I will continue to describe steps as if logged in as admin and submitting contact creation forms, but the same happens when submitting reports. 
- Open a form to create a new contact (type is irrelevant)
- Edit one of the fields, so the app marks the form as `edited`
- Open browser console

**Bug 1:**
- Click on any of the tabs

**What should happen**:
- You should get a popup saying `This form is not finished....` and not navigate away from the form. Clicking on "YES" should perform the navigation, "NO" should keep you on the same page.

**What actually happens**:
 - Chrome and Firefox: Errors in the console 
```
Transition Rejection($id: 13 type: 6, message: The transition errored, detail: TypeError: Cannot read property 'preventDefault' of undefined)
TypeError: Cannot read property 'preventDefault' of undefined
```

This is most likely connected to a recent upgrade of ui-router in webapp, and a switch from `$stateChangeStart` broadcast to `$transitions.onStart`.

**Bug 2:**
- Click on a contact in the LHS list

**What should happen**:
- You should get a popup saying `This form is not finished....` and not navigate away from the form. Clicking on "YES" should perform the navigation, "NO" should keep you on the same page.

**What actually happens**:
- Chrome: You get the popup, but the page underneath also navigates to the contact you clicked, without interacting with the popup.
- Firefox: Same console errors as in Bug 1

**Environment**
 Instance: _localhost_
 Browser: _Firefox 65, Chrome 72, Chromium 71_
 Client platform: _Ubuntu 18_
 App: _webapp_
 Version: _3.4.x, 3.5.x_

title: Registration transition should calculate dates relative to reported_date
body:
Currently, `registration` transition calculates three dates:
a. date of birth
b. last menstrual period
c. expected birth date

https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/3d4f54ec5772fc2bcc4f77c68d0e4ab26ad0ebf8/sentinel/src/transitions/registration.js#L221
https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/3d4f54ec5772fc2bcc4f77c68d0e4ab26ad0ebf8/sentinel/src/transitions/registration.js#L155

All of these dates are calculated in reference to the moment Sentinel processes the doc instead of (what seems logical to me) the doc's `reported_date`.

In an ideal world, Sentinel would never crash, never be misconfigured and should always process all docs in a timely manner. Sadly.... 

@abbyad @garethbowen I'm not sure if this is a bug or working as intended.

title: Add explanatory text about permissions to the admin app
body:
Add explanatory text about what the various permissions mean. Some are fairly self explanatory but others aren’t (for example, “can_view_unallocated_data_records”). It is hard for someone not intimately familiar with our app to understand what all of these mean. 

Suggest that a developer make the first pass looking at the code to see what each permission actually does. When the first pass is done, please loop in @jillrshah to help review the language.

A suggestion from Gareth is that we shouldn't even show the key in the UI - just the translated explanation. If we go this route, we might want to still have titles for each, but something that is more user friendly. For instance, "can_bulk_delete_reports" could be titled "Can bulk delete reports" with some explanatory text below describing what that means (i.e. “This feature allows a user to select more than one report at a time and delete the selected group in a single action.”)

title: Server side purge
body:
We recently added document purging on the client side which works really well for periodically deleting docs that are no longer needed. However because of the way it works it has to download the docs before it can determine if they should be purged. This will cause issues for people starting with a large number of docs, for example, if an existing user wipes the app or gets a new phone.

Instead, run the purge function on the server and store which users should purge the doc without deleting the doc itself - it must remain on the server. Existing clients will be told to purge the document from their local pouchdb. Exclude the document from the changes for those users so a new replication will never download it.

title: Angular $exceptionHandler too sensitive
body:
It appears that all UnhandledPromiseRejections are being pushed as feedback to the DB by the new $exceptionHandler, including network connection errors. 

**Steps to reproduce**:
 - Checkout latest master (3.5)
 - Deploy it - you don't need any configuration for this, just start the app 
 - I recommend deploying on an **empty throw-away DB**, as you're going to create thousands of identical feedback documents
 - Login as admin
 - Open the Dev tools network tab
 - Go to Messages tab
 - Keeping the network tab open, go offline (Via the network tab offline checkbox)
 - Click on the "Send message" button
 - Click "Cancel"

**What should happen**:
 - Your popup should go away and no new requests should appear in the network log

**What actually happens**:
 - The network tab quickly fills up with `_bulk_docs` requests that all fail (because we're offline). 
 - The `requests` counter should rise up quite quickly - don't wait too long, couple of seconds is enough
 - Go online again (Via the network tab offline checkbox)
 - It's very possible your browser will become unresponsive at this moment
 - Login to Fauxton and verify that you have **many** docs (depends on how long you stayed offline - my computer generates about 2000 in a couple of seconds), all feedback docs, all identical, all saying `Failed to fetch...`. 
 
**Some explanations**

 - Because our Modals are Promises that resolve when the user clicks "yes" and reject when the user clicks "no", not catching to the "no" qualifies as an unhandled promise rejection. We mostly do not catch "no"s if we don't want to do anything with them, so the above would be triggered on _most_ modals in the app. 
 - Clicking on the "No" button qualifies as an unhandled promise rejection, which the $exceptionHandler will pick up and try to post a feedback doc with it (which is another bug)
 - Because we are offline, the upload will fail, which will log another error which the $exceptionHandler will catch and will try to post a feedback doc with it  
 - Because we are offline, the upload will fail, which will log another error which the $exceptionHandler will catch and will try to post a feedback doc with it  
 - Because we are offline, the upload will fail, which will log another error which the $exceptionHandler will catch and will try to post a feedback doc with it  
 - You get the point

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/53957283-9f40f180-40e6-11e9-9178-d35eacf6e7c8.png)

 
 There are a number of other connection errors exception which are incorrectly reported as feedback, for example replication attempts of offline users when disconnected from the internet.
 
_Sincere apologies if the steps described above have crashed your browser/computer_

**Environment**:

- Instance: _local_
- Browser: _Firefox, Chrome, Chromium, irrelevant_
- Client platform: _Linux_
- App: _webapp_
- Version: _3.5_

title: Muso supervisors can't review mRDT reports while having a replication depth of 1
body:
## Some Background
Muso supervisors with a replication depth of 2 are forced to replication all families (clinics) and forms associated with those families. Many CHVs per supervisor * many familes per CHV yields an estimated 4000 home-visit forms per week for these supervisors. This causes performance problems. Performance of the app can be improved with purging, but replication for some users takes more than three days. To fix https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/5781, Muso is reducing the replication depth of supervisors to 1.

Muso is conducting an mRDT Trial starting April 1st in which supervisors need to review patient forms. These forms would require a replication depth of 3 (impossible), so Muso leverages the `needs_signoff` flag on reports. 

## Requirement
The needs_signoff flag only works for reports which are one level deeper than the user's replication depth. With a replication depth of 1, Muso supervisors cannot review a report at depth 3. 

For the April 1st trial, Muso is setting a replication depth of 2 for the mRDT supervisor (one user only) and configuring purging with aggressively supervisor-specific rules. However, this won't scale well for the mRDT scaleup in August as all supervisors would be hindered by multi-day replication times with the replication depth of 2. 

Muso needs a solution which would allow a replication depth of 1 for a user which can also review reports at depth 3.

title: Support a Muso Target - % of families which have received 2 home visits this month
body:
In Muso-land, a "home visit" can occur up to once per day per family. For any given family on any give day, the home visit has occured if either a) any member of the family has a report created on that day (which also meets some specific criteria that isn't important for this bug); or b) the family (clinic) has a home visit report created on that day.

A primary goal for Muso's CHWs is to visit every family twice per month. Muso has requested that a target be written which tracks this goal for CHWs. This number can't be calculated by inspecting the reports for any single contact, it is an aggregation of information from many contacts or many emitted target instances. Since nools does not preserved any state information from one contact to the next, I'm unsure how to build this target in either declarative config or the older nools.rules system.

I suspect we need a product change to support this requirement from Muso.

[Target code for total number of home visits](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/blob/muso-declarative/muso_declarative/targets.js#L3)

title: 4750 Moves selected to redux store
body:
# Description

Continuing on from [these PRs](https://github.com/medic/medic/pulls?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Apr+is%3Aclosed+4750), this PR moves `selected` to the redux store which involves a significant number of changes (ran into a lot of problems with this).

Points to note:
- There some slightly weird logic flows in the code below. For now I think the best approach is to migrate to redux leaving functionality exactly as it is, and then potentially rethink some of the logic once the migration is finished in order to help with a) getting the migration done quickly and b) diagnosing bugs that are inevitably going to be introduced by this migration
- Introduction of **selectors**. Selectors provide an abstracted way of accessing the store which I've found beneficial for two reasons (read more [here](https://github.com/reduxjs/reselect#reselect)):
  1. If you change the organisation of the store significantly, you can update the selectors without having to update all the components that use those bits of store
  2. They're useful for computing derived data. Memoised selectors mean computing derived data only happens when the underlying store data actually changes, nifty.
- I somehow missed that `$scope.selected` was never actually defined in `inbox.js`, only in `contacts.js` etc, meaning that they were all actually separate variables. In redux they have now become one variable which shouldn't be a problem as it's cleared by every "module" (contacts, reports, etc) when initiated, but it's getting to the point with this redux work where reducers should probably be split out into modules so they can be split out again into separate variables.
