title: Creating / syncing meta db-s fails when db name is not "medic"
body:
When you deploy medic app and use a db name that is not `medic`, creation and replication of user meta dbs doesn't work, having all sorts of effects on the app.

For online users, which query the DB directly, loading reports fails and the console is riddled with replication failures. 
For offline users, loading reports works as the queryied DB exists locally, but replicating upstream will fail. 

The reason is that webapp builds the meta db name based on the main db name and adds a suffix: `<main-db-name>-user-<username>-meta`, while API hardcodes the meta db names to `medic-user-<username>-meta` both in `routing` and in the `user-db` service. 

Since we're intending to use meta db-s for more than storing read docs (telemetry, feedback, etc) we should make sure this data is uploaded correctly.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/54440080-b1eca380-4742-11e9-946c-19cf716890b8.png)

title: Update config/standard after medic-conf breaking changes
body:
*Please don't merge this until medic-conf v2.0.0 is merged and available*

# Description

Hey @eljhkrr and @derickl! I've proposed a few breaking changes to the declarative configuration system in the medic-conf repository. Instead of making these changes backwards compatible, I'd simply like to update all declarative configuration projects.

You can read about each of the changes I'm making [here](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Amuso-config). But to summarize the big changes briefly:

* I'm trying to standardize the contracts that we use to pass data from the application code into the webapp. So instead of each file having a custom contract (like "this file should declare one specific variable name x" or "this file should be an array" or "this file should return an object defining three attributes". All files now pass data through the standard `module.exports` pattern. I'm hoping this will crisp up the expected behavior of code, and allow code to be more unit testable since you can now use the file in unit tests directly.
* I'm trying to converge the CHT code onto the JavaScript community's standard patterns for sharing code between files. So code from shared libraries now export the data which can be used in other files. This adds some boilerplate - but hopefully that will be mitigated when we support ES6 in the near future. I'm trying to position us so that in a future change, we can include third-party libraries (underscore or moment) and we can share code between projects more easily through the arbitrary use of `require`. 
* I find it hard to understand (and hard to document) when functions are overloaded with multiple definitions depending on the value of other data in the declarative system. For example, when `events[n].dueDate` sometimes receives `(c, event)` and sometimes receives `(r, event)` and  sometimes receives `(r, event, scheduledTaskIdx)`. I'm doing an interface change so that interfaces remain constant. As such, there are minor parameter changes to `tasks.events[n].dueDate`, `tasks.actions[n].modifyContent`, `targets.emitCustom`, and `targets.date`.

I'm sending this review early, before it is ready to merge. I'd love our feedback and thoughts, as well as Elijah's assistance testing this for regressions ([code](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/tree/v2)).

title: Investigate memory footprint of instances emitted by Targets
body:
For each target, for each value counted, two identical objects are held in medic's memory and a third is potentially held within Nools. Each object is roughly ~250 bytes in size.  So for example, if you're seeing a target which shows a count of "200" or which shows a percent of 50% ("100 out of 200"), there are 400 objects in memory for this (~100kb). Nools may also be storing a copy of this, because in practice I'm seeing around ~1kb of heap allocated per target per value counted (would be ~400 kb on heap in this example). 

For a Muso user with 700 reports, I see a delta of 5-7MBs of heap allocation when turning off all targets. For users with a large document count or projects with many targets, I suspect this could end up being quite significant and may warrant further investigation and measurement. 

First copy stored is this [emissions](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/rules-engine.js#L90) object in RulesEngine. The second copy is this [instances](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/target-generator.js#L66) object in TargetGenerator.

If this is indeed significant, some performance improvements we might consideration:

1. We are duplicating the stored data in both RulesEngine and TargetGenerator, can we share it? Does Nools have a copy we can use instead of storing this ourselves?
1. We store all emitted instances in RulesEngine, even for users who don't have permissions to `can_view_analytics`.
1. RulesEngine stores all emitted instances, even if they don't end up being relevant to the target's count. If we moved the logic in TargetGenerator's `isRelevant` function into medic-conf, we wouldn't have to store so many unused emitted instances.
1. Each time an instance is emitted, we recalculate the state of the target. This makes an O(n^2) operation and may have a noticeable impact on replication and purging.
1. Currently, the data in the instance is limited to just counting a single object. `{ pass: true }`, but we could emit something which contains a count: `{ count: 5, pass: 3 }`. This could significantly reduce the number of instances as well as improving code clarity in the declarative configuration system.

diff --git a/98793c4709528cf3bfcf08f57efd38abdbf6ea51 b/e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391
index 98793c4..e69de29 100644
--- a/98793c4709528cf3bfcf08f57efd38abdbf6ea51
+++ b/e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391
@@ -1,3 +0,0 @@
[-[high] Regular Expression Denial of Service for tough-cookie (#525) in .-]
[-[high] Regular Expression Denial of Service for minimatch (#118) in sentinel/src/lib/pupil-]
[-[high] Insufficient Entropy for cryptiles (#720) in tests/scalability-]
>> Exited with code: 1.
>> Error executing child process: Error: Process exited with code 1.

Instead of failing, if we get this specific message we should wait and retry a couple of times.

title: Countdown timer does not respect custom timer value
body:
The countdown timer is always using the default time of 60, even when set as shown in https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/1531#issuecomment-155388612

Here is a sample XLSForm and corresponding XForm: [timer.zip](https://github.com/medic/medic/files/3006010/timer.zip)


**Steps to reproduce**:
 - Create a form with a non-default timer (eg set to `9` seconds)
 - Open form and tap on timer

**What should happen**:
 - Timer should have a 9 countdown before completion

**What actually happens**:

**Environment**:

- Instance: standard.dev, gamma.dev
- Browser: Chrome 72
- Client platform: Windows
- App: webapp
- Version: 2.18.0-beta.1 on standard.dev, and 3.2.1 on gamma.dev

title: UHC metrics are incongruous between contacts and analytics tab due to month_start_date
body:
Muso has several UHC-specific targets which report metrics which overlap with the data on the UHC-enabled contacts tab. For example, they track "total number of home visits this month" and "% of families which have received >= 2 home visits this month" in the analytics tab.

The UHC data on the contacts tab reports on a monthly period from the 26th to the 25th (eg. Feb 26th to March 25th). This is controlled via a configurable "month_start_date" in app_settings.  At the same time, the same data is reported on the targets tab from the 1st to the last of the month (eg. Feb 1st to March 1st). This is not configurable.

The two metrics aren't aggregating the same information and appear broken.
* On March 1st, the contacts tab reports "10 home visits for Bob's family" and the analytics tab reports "0 home visits this month". 
* On March 26th, the contact's tab tab reports "0 home visits" for everybody and the analytics tab reports "350 home visits this month".

This is two tabs for the same user at the same time:
![Screenshot from 2019-03-27 09-20-59](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9014751/55093478-b0d84200-5071-11e9-899f-fa4e9f1a08c4.png)

title: Documentation tooling
body:
It would be cool if we could add an automatic documentation generation tool into our development flow. This would help newcomers as well as (hopefully!) help us to write good code-local documentation.

It should understand some kind of JS-friendly comment-based documentation (like [JSDoc](http://usejsdoc.org/about-getting-started.html)), and use that to generate some readable documentation (e.g. html or markdown) that we can store somewhere and refer to.

Whether or not that storage is part of the each commit (e.g. it gets run as part of Grunt and updates a git-commitable location) or whether we run it manually occasionally (e.g. on every release) to be stored elsewhere is up for debate.

It would also be useful if it understood Angular's conventions, so it could intelligently link controllers to services and so on.

title: Measure and if possible improve CouchDB GET performance via API
body:
While doing some performance benchmarks (see Context below) I noticed that attachment GETs are really slow for what they are.

This may be true for all GETs, and could be due to our new security code making sure you're allowed to GET the thing you're asking for.

We should measure the performance of GET requests (and honestly authenticated interactions with api in general), work out if we're adding overhead and how much, and see if there are ways we can improve the code to remove those overheads.

Obvious things would be caching certain critical pieces of data, though it's unclear what we could easily cache (apart from UserCtx). At the very least we should understand what is going on.

Context: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kXjsF-orndz0-V5UFf_Esx5J-ogeQ6_tALCwE1K0tvA/edit#heading=h.29bkt8nfi7kw

title: SSL + DNS stack for on-device testing
body:
# Description

#5340 

This is an unfortunate barrier to on-device testing which comes from service workers. Run `grunt exec:mobile-service-stack` to spin up a DNS server + SSL proxy, then follow the steps to use it on your Android device. This process enables secure testing via https://medic.dev.

Would be great if we didn't need a DNS -- here are things I couldn't get working:

1. Test using the developer's IP address (as before), but secure the connection using a generated certificate for that IP. Chrome gives ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID.
1. Testing via the developer's machine-name instead of needing DNS. This works on some routers which provide the functionality, but not for all networks (eg. android tethering).


Interested in other vectors to solve this. I think all I have left is @garethbowen's magic sauce in the Android wrapper as described in the linked issue. As-yet unexplored.

Can we start by having somebody follow the steps in the README.md and see if this is reasonably easy to follow? @SCdF, I think you offered to try it out in Slack at one point. If you don't still have time, let me know and I'll find someone.

title: Expired tasks don't disappear from the Tasks tab when they expire
body:
1. Configure a task which will emit with a dueDate of today, and an expiry date of tomorrow.
1. Set your clock to 11:55pm, refresh the page, navigate to the 'tasks' tab and see the task.
1. Wait 5 minutes, and you should see the dueDate "today" change to "yesterday" and turn red.
1. Set your clock to tomorrow + 11:55pm, refresh the page, and view the task.

Expected: After 5 minutes, this task should disappear because it has expired.
Observed: Wait 5 minutes, and you will see the dueDate "tomorrow" change to "2 days ago". Refresh the tab and the expired task will disappear.

There is some [code in LiveList which is run at midnight](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/live-list.js#L543) which refreshes the description of the task. There is an expectation that we should maybe also remove expired tasks here.

title: Fix UHC styling when using both UHC and muting at the same time
body:
There is a bug/oversight in our UI styling when using both UHC and muting features at the same time. 

**What it currently looks like:** 
When a contact is muted and is displaying a grey icon in the main contacts list, the UHC date last visited and visits per month text is still styled red. This is confusing as it sends conflicting signals to the user. The red says “look at me, I’m important”, while the grey icon and muted status is meant to say “don’t worry about me, I’m not as important”.

**What it should look like:**
- If a contact is muted, the date last visited text should always be colored black, even if over 30 days.
- If a contact is muted, the number of visits per month (right side) is always grey, no matter if the visit count is 0, 1, 2, or 2+.
- If a contact is muted, the number of visits per month (right side) does not have a warning sign icon associated with it, no matter if the visit count is 0, 1, 2, or 2+.

**Mockups**
On the left is the current problematic styling. On the right is the desired styling.

![Screen Shot 2019-04-19 at 9 12 45 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/56432724-55b9f980-6283-11e9-9761-e359d5816417.png)


IMPORTANT: Another option could be to remove all UHC information from muted contacts entirely (don't display the date last visited or visits this month at all for those who are muted). But this should only be done if we are also able to accomplish #5596. If the muted contacts remain intermingled amongst active contacts then I think it makes sense to keep the UHC information, as it explains the sorting method.

title: Sort muted contacts to the bottom of the contacts list
body:
Right now muted contacts remain on the main contacts list, intermingled amongst active contacts, the only difference being that their icons are styled grey.

Our initial proposal for muting was that we would like to collect all of the muted contacts in a separate folder that lives at the bottom of the list. However this posed some technical challenges and we dropped it from the muting MVP.

@dianabarsan  said theoretically we could re-sort the contacts, but this would require updating the form that lists the people, and all phones would have to re-index their data.

An alternative could be sorting muted contacts to the bottom of the list ONLY when the list is sorted by “date last visited”. In UHC mode the default sorting is configurable by project, and any UHC user can go in at any time and toggle the sorting back and forth between “by date last visited” and “alphabetically”. But if _most_ UHC projects set their default sort to date last visited (Muso does), and if _most_ users typically leave it on the default sort, this solution could help most users in most cases.

Would be nice if devs could explore the potential solution described above (which would only help UHC projects) and/or any other ways to sort the muted contacts to the bottom of the list, which might potentially work across all projects.

title: Integration with Africa's Talking SMS aggregator
body:
A new project EBS wants to use feature phones and SMS instead of smartphones and data. Usually we use medic-gateway running on android to send and receive SMS using medic-api APIs, but it has some issues including being dropped from the play store, the app going to sleep, low throughput, high latency, etc. It would be much better to use a specialized third party cloud hosted aggregator instead. For this project we've chosen [Africa's Talking](https://africastalking.com/sms/twowaysms).

1. Create a new routine to send SMS via Africa's Talking (both immediate messages such as auto replies, and scheduled messages generated periodically).
2. Create a new API (potentially multiple endpoints) that Africa's Talking will call when an SMS is received.
3. Create a new API to update the status of outgoing messages as they are delivered.
4. This integration must be disabled by default, and all the account information must be configurable.

Africa's Talking provides a sandbox mode you can use during development and testing, and have support if required. The also have an [npm SDK package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/africastalking) which exposes a simple API to use, as well as tutorials on how to integrate.

There will likely be more integrations with other providers at a later date so consider refactoring the gateway and Africa's Talking integrations to use shared services where possible to make reuse easier for the next integration.

@newtewt prototyped an integration using expressjs which almost worked and may be useful as a starting point.

title: Add feature to create a place via SMS
body:
You can create a patient using the `add_patient` trigger on the [registration transition](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/sentinel/src/transitions/registration.js#L349) but there's no way to create a place via SMS so if you want to register a new household you need to do that in the webapp before registering the patients.

Add the ability to register a place via SMS at the right place in the hierarchy. The place may have a unique `place_id` generated allowing contacts to be created as children of the place.

Example workflow:

1. CHP: `RF Smith family` (where RF is a JSON form for registering families).
2. Response: `Smith family registered with place ID 11111`
3. CHP: `R 11111 John`
4. Response: `John added to the Smith family with patient ID 11112`
5. CHP: `R 11111 Jane`
6. etc...

title: 6042 fix case sensitive issue
body:
# Description
The immunization visit form (form: C_IMM) submitted from collect app has value `Yes` for a immunization received, i.e. `"received_bcg": "Yes"`. In the code, `addImmunizations(): vaccines_received['received_' + dose[0]] === 'yes'` checks for `yes`. And, since `Yes` and `yes` are different in case, the condition card is not getting updated for the immunization visit forms submitted from the collect app. To overcome this case-sensitive issue, `toLowerCase()` is used in the comparison in the relevant function. It is related to [GH Issue 6402](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6042#issuecomment-483633418).

title: Changing user profile language prevents user from changing back to original language
body:
**Steps to reproduce**:
1. Log in as national or district admin
1. Go to user settings > Edit user profile > Language
1. Select a different language from what has already been set i.e. change from English to Swahili
1. Navigate away from user settings
1. Go to user settings > Edit user profile > Language
1. Select the language that had originally been set and apply i.e. change from Swahili to English

**What should happen**:
 - The language should change back to English from Swahili

**What actually happens**:
 - The language doesn't change back to English but can change to other languages other than the original language.

**Environment**:

- Instance: villagehealthworks-burundi.app.medicmobile.org
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.4.0

title: Broken functionality after upgrade to 3.4 with custom locales
body:
_Supported languages do not show on the languages tab of languages settings, specific to webapps upgraded to 3.4.0_.

**Steps to reproduce**:
 - _Login as admin on an upgraded instance (not a fresh 3.4.0, but an upgraded webapp), e.g. `pih-malawi.dev`_
 - _Go to App Settings > Languages > Languages_

**What should happen**:
 - _Supported locales should be listed on the page, where one can set a default language among other operations. See screenshot below._

title: JavaScript errors and crash stacks not logged to the console
body:
**Describe the bug**
Not all JavaScript errors and crash stacks are reported to the console.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open `webapp/webapp/src/js/controllers/inbox.js` in an editor and delete `Auth` from the ngInjection list (line 24).
1. Rebuild app
1. Login to the webapp

**Observed behavior**
The console has no errors.

**Expected behavior**
This is a basic scripting error in which we are using an undefined variable. The app fails to load (expected) but there should be an error in the console explaining why.



I think this bug is important and labelled it Priority 1 because these console errors are often our only way to investigate/understand live-site issues on the client.

title: Add Zapier webhook to Travis
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently we have Travis CI notifications in a group Slack channel for all failures, and when the success status changes. These notifications occur for all branches, which becomes overly noisy in Slack.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
From internal discussion the first phase would be to reduce noise by only showing failures and changes of status of the master branch. Optionally, we could notify only the user in question.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively we could disable Slack notifications altogether, and rely on email notifications to individuals, otherwise have the notifications in another channel altogether, and they could monitor that channel with notifications for their name/handle.

title: Ability to calculate how many tasks are shown and completed by users
body:
To improve our impact we must first measure our impact.

One of our major features is tasks and we make it very difficult to measure how many tasks are being shown to users and how many tasks are being completed. This is due to tasks being ephemeral and generated on the phone so server side analytics queries don't have access to this information. Instead the impact team create custom queries based on the configuration of each project but this is error prone and time consuming.

One solution would be to write tasks to the database and replicate to couchdb but this could have a potentially serious performance impact.

Consider various implementations and analyse the performance impacts of each before implementation.

title: Calculate data for DHIS2 reports
body:
Every month CHPs are expected to submit a DHIS2 report which records information such as "Number of households visited". We have enough information to automate the calculation of much of this data so we can make the reporting much more efficient and less error prone by prepopulating the form. Note that as well as the aggregate data we also need to be able to view the items that contributed to this total (#5660), using the above example we need to show not only the number of households visited, but also the names of the households.

It may be possible to configure nools to generate a task which has collects all the data and passes it to the form using global variables to store data as the families are being processed.

Alternatively we could create a new doc type to store this data and create a new instance each month on the phone.

Analyse the implementations and prove and/or implement the correct approach.

title: Ability to configure forms access based on hierarchy
body:
_*User story*_
As LG scales up and work on many experiment projects, it’s becoming increasing critical to have a way to `dynamically configure which CHVs access certain workflows` and who don’t have access. Sometimes CHVs participating in experiments are not segregated in a clear way like per branch. We can have sample CHVs from multiple branches.

We also need an intuitive way for non technical staff to assign and de-assign workflows/forms to CHVs unlike the current method where we put CHV uuids on the contact summary to indicate CHVs eligible for a certain experiment

_*Suggested solution*_
Adding an array of forms on the place object. These forms should be visible to everyone below the hierarchy. If you don’t want a form visible to everyone, you configure it down the hierarchy on the relevant place object. Check the example below
```
{
    "name":"…..",
    "uuid":"………",
    "forms": ["assessment.xml", "pregnancy.xml", ….],
    …
}
```
We can have a web tool (maybe on the admin panel) where a non-technical user can assign forms to branches or individual CHVs

title: Cache the path accessed from _rewrite
body:
# Description

Another regression from #5361. The android app navigates the user to `/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/` and does not use the root url. To support offline mode, we need to ensure that a redirect from that rewrite page to root is cached.

I see a few options here: 

1. Existing service workers - The `appcache-upgrade.html` could register the existing service-worker and redirect once registration completes. During an upgrade this would load all of the app's resources during an empty page and is not ideal.
1. Appcache - Given that we have the appropriate manifest already in place (required for the upgrade process), I think this is the easiest and is the fix I pursued here.
1. New service worker - Could also do this. But it's a new file, a new build step, and a bit of a registration process. If things go wrong on this page, we have no feedback mechanic.
1. I hoped a `301` permanent redirect would work here. But this really complicates how we clear the appcache during the upgrade to service workers.

#3986 

Nasty business in the app since we now navigate to `/rewire`, get an appcached version of that page, redirect to `/`, and get a serviceworker cached version of that page. So I'm coupling this with a build-time flag in the app to avoid this for partners when they migrate to >3.5.
https://github.com/medic/medic-android/pull/70

title: Update apps to use local shared-libs
body:
We use `npm pack` to zip `api` and `sentinel` and attach them to our build ddoc as part of build process. We also use a collection of scoped (`@medic/<library>`) [shared libraries](https://github.com/medic/medic/tree/master/shared-libs)  across our apps.

title: Schedules are not cleared with Unicode form codes
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reported in `medic-projects`: https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6366

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load standard config on an instance.
1. Replace "N" form with "क" (do this in the form definition and `registrations` config, alternatively you can duplicate the form and schedule from another form)
3. Submit your new "क" form, wait until your report is processed and patient created. The report should have one scheduled task. 
4. For the new patient, submit a "P" form.

**Expected behavior**
After your "P" report is processed, the previous "क" report scheduled task should be cleared.

**What actually happens**
The scheduled task from your "क" report is still scheduled. 

**Environment**
- Instance: any 3.4, 3.5 instance
- App: api, sentinel
- Version: 3.4, 3.5

**Additional context**
When validating whether a report is a valid registration, we extract the form code from the document `form` property with `/^[^\w-]*([\w-]+)[^\w-]*$/` [here](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/shared-libs/registration-utils/src/index.js#L3).
In javascript, `\w` does not match non-ASCII unicode even when using the `u` flag. 
Using the `\p` metacharacter along with the `u` flag instead works, like:
`/^[^\p{L}\p{N}_-]*([\p{L}\p{N}_-]+)[^\p{L}\p{N}_-]*$/u`

title: Webapp doesn't support languages that are not pluralized by `make-plural`
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reports fail to load when the user language isn't pluralized by `make-plural`. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Install 3.5 (or 3.4)
2. Create a new language with a code that is not-existent or is not pluralized by `make-plural`. For example "rn". 
I prefer to copy whole contents of a translation file that already exists and just change the `code` and `_id` fields to match.
3. Login as an online user to the instance and change your language to "rn". Go to reports. **Refresh**
4. Observe that no reports load on the LHS and translations are missing from some of the filters.

**Expected behavior**
Reports LHS should load. 

**Logs**
There are no errors logged in the console.

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/58900966-dbe1b080-8708-11e9-9318-cf1a82afb049.png)


**Environment**
- Instance: local, [live instance](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6310)
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Linux
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.4, 3.5 (possibly earlier)

**Additional context**
There are no errors visible in the console because `angular-translate` [deliberately ignores all translation loading errors](https://github.com/angular-translate/angular-translate/blob/master/src/service/translate.js#L1950):
```
langPromises[key]['finally'](function () {
    clearNextLangAndPromise(key);
})['catch'](angular.noop); // we don't care about errors (clearing)
``` 
If I change the source to actually log the error, replacing `angular.noop` with `console.error`:
```
Error: Localisation function not found for locale "rn"
    at Object.get (plurals.js:31)
    at new MessageFormat (messageformat.js:37)
    at Object.setLocale (angular-translate-interpolation-messageformat:121)
    at eachInterpolator (angular-translate.js:1633)
    at Object.forEach (angular.js:401)
    at useLanguage (angular-translate.js:1638)
    at angular-translate.js:2324
    at processQueue (angular.js:17914)
    at angular.js:17962
    at Scope.$digest (angular.js:19075)
```
We plug in the `message-format` interpolation to handle plurals, which in turn uses `make-plural` library.
We wait for the `$translate` to be `ready` [before we load forms](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/controllers/inbox.js#L421), 
and we wait for forms to be loaded [before we load reports in the LHS](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/controllers/reports.js#L471).
We also wait for `$translate` to be `ready` to load report filters.

`$translate` throws the error before broadcasting the "ready" event, so forms never load, so reports never load.

`make-plural` covers lots of languages, but not all. "rn" is a valid language code for Kirundi.
[Link to the source of `make-plural` covered languages](https://github.com/eemeli/make-plural/blob/master/packages/plurals/umd/plurals.js)

title: Makes replication _all_docs requests quicker
body:
When replicating down, after receiving a batch of changes, PouchDB will iterate them to comprise a list of docs that are on their 1st revision. If any are found, it would try to get them with an `_all_docs?include_docs=true` request, presumably as a performance shortcut.
Once it receives the results, all of the docs that are not retrieved (for any reason) or have attachments or have since been edited or have conflicts, will be retrieved with the next `_bulk_get` request. 

The `_all_docs` calls are particularly expensive, as the implementation composes the list of all allowed doc ids that the user is allowed to see and compose a response based on that.
While this implementation is correct for generalized `_all_docs` requests (requesting `_all_docs` without parameters is expected to return the full list of existent docs stubs), we could improve it for the specific case of replication requests (that use `keys` and `include_docs=true`) parameters to actually request the docs and run the view map queries over the results to filter the ones the user is allowed to see - similar to how we filter `_bulk_get` requests.

title: The `initial_replication_date` in info docs is always `unknown`
Improves performance of replication _all_docs requests
body:
# Description

During replication, PouchDB will always request with `keys` and `include_docs=true`. 
Since we would already run the query with `include_docs`, it's faster to run the authorization methods over the resulted docs to filter the allowed ones versus compiling the list of allowed doc ids and pre-filtering the requested ids. 

Running locally, using the seed data (from gamma.dev): performance difference: 

| Instance | Initial replication | Replicating 100 new docs from the server |
|----------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| master   | 40.5s               | 3.02s                                    |
| this PR  | 25.5s               | 2.21s                                    |

title: Immunization Condition Card not getting updated as per Collect Immunization Form submission
body:
Description

The [Immunization Condition Card](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6042#issuecomment-478858331) is not getting updated as per the [Immunization report](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/config/standard/forms/collect/c_imm.xlsx) submitted from the collect app. As per the code in `contact-summary-extras.js`, the card gets updated if the value of corresponding immunization key is set to `yes` in the document. i.e. https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/config/standard/contact-summary-extras.js#L249 But the document created in couchdb corresponding to an immunization form submission has values `Yes/No`, hence the check `vaccines_received['received_' + dose[0]] === 'yes';` fails and the card is not updated. To patch this issue, the code can be updated as [vaccines_received['received_' + dose[0]].toLowerCase() === 'yes';](https://github.com/medic/medic/pull/5615/files/9bff39a83f0f1630075f7e492fcf1dfbd7c50c8f#diff-084981c49a350848a9d6eecd777a9d23 ) but it does not answer the question that why the immunization report created in couchdb have values `Yes/No` instead of `yes/no` as set in the [Immunization Form](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/config/standard/forms/collect/c_imm.xlsx).

Investigation

The value `yes/no` is getting translated according to the translation key in the translation file (message-en.properties, message-ne.properties etc.). If translation file has entry of `yes=Yes` and `no=No`, then the `translationCache` gets set correspondingly in `config.js`: https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/api/src/config.js#L81-L92 And then, when the immunization collect form submission is parsed with [smsparser](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/api/src/services/report/smsparser.js#L174) it returns `Yes` and `No` as the translated value of `yes` and `no`, and the same is set in the couchdb document. https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/api/src/services/report/smsparser.js#L159-L178

Resolution

There could be multiple ways to resolve this: 1. Change `yes=Yes` to `yes=yes` and `no=No` to `no=no` in all the [translation files](https://github.com/medic/medic/tree/master/config/standard/translations). 2. Do not translate the `value of string` while parsing i.e. change `return config.translate(raw);` to `return raw;`. https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/api/src/services/report/smsparser.js#L178 3. Find out what can be changed in `config.js` https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/api/src/config.js#L119-L122 Please let me know your views on resolution of this issue. @abbyad @medic/development-team

title: The POE export script incorrectly detects invalid placeholders
body:
**Describe the bug**
We recently introduced a script to export our translations from POE into the repo for inclusion in the release. One of the parts of this tries to detect when someone has accidentally translated or typoed a placeholder (eg: `{{contact.nme}}`). This works well mostly but is showing a lot of false negatives.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install the POE script following the instructions in [the README](https://github.com/medic/medic/tree/master/scripts/poe)
2. Go to `/ddocs/medic/_attachments/translations`
3. Run `poe export .`
4. See a bunch of errors, eg:

```
FAILURE: messages-loz.properties: Translation key messages.v.report_accepted on line 752 has placeholders that do not match those of messages-en.properties
FAILURE: messages-ne.properties: Translation key contact.primary_contact_name on line 426 has placeholders that do not match those of messages-en.properties
FAILURE: messages-es.properties: Translation key contact.primary_contact_name on line 426 has placeholders that do not match those of messages-en.properties
```

**Expected behavior**
It should only error when the placeholder is actually invalid. 

**Environment**
- Instance: localhost
- Client platform: Ubuntu
- App: webapp script
- Version: master

**Additional context**
The workaround is to ignore the errors - the script still does the export and the files can be committed regardless.

**Fix**

Examples of false negatives:

- Not using a placeholder that the reference language (English) uses - it may make sense in some languages to omit a placeholder altogether and this is valid.
- Using a placeholder multiple times or in a different order than the reference language does.
- Using a placeholder that does work but isn't used in the reference language.

We need to build a list of valid placeholders. Currently that list is only what is provided in the English translation, but that's incomplete. I think we need to include some sort of allow list of placeholders which are valid even if they're not included in the English translation.

title: Incorrect XLSForm meta data values in Enketo
body:
In XLSForm there are [keywords for meta data](http://xlsform.org/en/#metadata), some of which are relevant and available in our app with Enketo. Of those some provide incorrect values, such as `start` and `end` which always give midnight GMT for the given day. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Upload the [`meta` form](https://github.com/medic/medic/files/3340296/meta.zip)
2. Open the `meta` form
3. See the incorrect values as notes
4. Submit the form and see the same incorrect values being saved

**Expected behavior**
The `start` and `end` values should have the time included with the date.

To maintain consistency with XLSForm it would be nice to also have the user's `phonenumber`, `username`, `email`. That said, those fields are less relevant in our context, and are available via `inputs` as a workaround.

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/60361615-ae58f180-99ac-11e9-82bd-fc802f051be0.png)

```json
  "fields": {
    "start": "2019-06-27T20:00:00.000-04:00",
    "end": "2019-06-27T20:00:00.000-04:00",
    "today": "2019-06-27",
    "deviceid": "deviceid not found",
    "subscriberid": "subscriberid not found",
    "simserial": "simserial not found",
    "phonenumber": "phonenumber not found",
    "username": "username not found",
    "email": "email not found",
    "n": "",
    "meta": {
      "instanceID": "uuid:f31d64b7-19ba-43c1-8e34-657c050c81a3"
    },
    "deprecatedID": ""
  },
```

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev.medicmobile.org
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.6 (pre-release), also tested on 2.18

**Additional context**
Being consistent with XLSForm keywords makes it easier for partners to build their own forms. In this case, a partner wanted to track the `start` and `end` time to see how long it takes users to complete a form. Alternatively, the `once(now())` could have been used to get the start time, but that would be a bit of a hack and we don't yet support `once()`. Also, having ODK events and actions (https://github.com/enketo/enketo/issues/300) could eventually be used for this as well, but doesn't fully override the need for supporting the XLSForm meta fields.

Also, this issue highlights the need to document differences with XLSForm and ODK XForm standards. If updating [the documentation](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/configuration/forms.md#custom-xpath-functions) is not covered in this issue we should create a new one for that.

Another part is that many layers of the code (services, controllers, actions, shared-libs) can all query the database. title: Show a prompt when we detect the user is logged out
body:
In 3.6.0 we implemented a [feature](https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/3919) to detect if the user's session has expired and redirect them to the login page. This cleans up a bunch of issues where the app started behaving strangely with no notification. As @dianabarsan [noted](https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/3919#issuecomment-503955033)...

> Every type of automatic (background) replication will redirect any type of user to the login page without warning and without being triggered by the user interacting with the app. If it's not too difficult, I think it would be much less intrusive to show a popup that informs the user that they have been logged out - similar to the one we use to prompt users to refresh once the app is updated.

Improve the current handling by showing a popup with an appropriate warning.

1. If the user chooses to login, redirect to the login page.
2. If the user cancels out of the popup, then show it again in some time (roughly 5 minutes?).
3. If the user doesn't interact with the popup at all for one minute then assume they've stepped away from the keyboard and not currently in the middle of a task and redirect them to the login page.

title: Make it clear that tasks can be completed anywhere in the window, not just on the due date
body:
Through design feedback sessions with CHWs in the PA pilot, we learned that they believe tasks could only be completed on their actual due date, not before, and not after.  This was consistent across almost all CHWs we interacted with. CHWs expressed that if they were at a household and noticed that there was a task due for another member of the household the next day, that they would come back the next day to complete that task, rather than completing it in the same visit. 

This has the potential to be a huge time/resource drain for CHWs and likely contributes to observed low task completion. 

The "due date" language seemed to be particularly confusing.

title: Muso's mRDT supervisor tasks cannot resolve
body:
For Muso's mRDT supervisor workflows:
* A CHW creates a report with `needs_signoff: true` for patient C.
* Supervisor A logs in with replication depth 1. The report replicates to their phone only because of `needs_signoff`. They can review/approve the report.
* A task triggers action from Supervisor A. Clicking the task makes a second report indicating the supervisor has followed up.

**Expected Behaviour**
The action of the task should be able to resolve the task.

**Observed Behaviour**
The logic controlling tasks is scoped to only access data for one contact at a time. Therefore the report which is created must be assigned with a `patient_id` which is equal to the owner of the original report (patient C). 

Because of the replication depth, patient C is not present on the device and the app crashes when building a ContactSummary. The user sees no error (only an infinite spinner), but does this appears in the console:

```
Error: Document not found: cb547802-75f6-48ef-bce0-0a28539789d0
    at lineage-model-generator.js:26
```

**Second Problem**
If the follow-up report were to be properly associated with Patient C, the task would still be impossible to resolve. This is because reports associated with contacts which are not on the device are not grouped under the same contact (even though the associated contact id is the same) - each report is given a new unique anonymous contact, so they are never in scope at the same time for the task logic.




More details about these scenarios and other issues contained in: https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6519 and https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/issues/205

title: Allow mRDT Supervisor Tasks to resolve based on multiple needs_signoff reports
body:
# Description

Because of replication depth, the `contact_id` for a task's action may not be present on the device. This change makes it so enketo does a "best effort" to inject contact data when none is present, instead of throwing when building a ContactSummary.

Reports associated with contacts which are not on the device are not grouped under the same contact even when the associated contact id is the same. This updates RulesEngine to group reports by contact id in such cases.

title: Warn offline users before replicating too many docs

# Description

Adds `/api/v1/users-info` endpoint which 
- returns the number of docs a user will replicate and a `warn` flag if this number exceeds the recommended limit. 
- when queried as an offline user, returns the requester doc count.
- when queried as an online user, requires `facility_id` and `role` params, plus an optional `contact_id` param (either GET or POST). 
- is queried as a new step in `webapp` bootstrapper. When resulting `warn` flag is truthy, the user has to confirm to actually continue bootstrapping and start replication. Cancelling redirects to login.
- is queried as a new step in `admin` user creation/updating. When resulting `warn` flag is truthy, a warning message is displayed. The admin would need to click on "Submit" the 2nd time to actually create or update the user document. 

Once an hour, API will log warnings of users that have replicated more than 10 000 docs. 
Updates `webapp` bootstrapper to display correct doc count progression, even when interrupted.

title: Make replication _bulk_docs requests quicker
body:
Similarly to https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5759, the current implementation of `_bulk_docs` filtering for offline users makes use of getting all the allowed doc ids in order to determine whether the user is allowed to edit an existent doc. 
For large users, getting the allowed doc ids can be quite time consuming. 
Instead of getting all allowed ids, we can do an `_all_docs` to get all existent docs that the user is trying to update and run the view map functions over the results in order to filter the allowed ones.

title: Display page tab text labels even on mobile view, whenever there are 3 or fewer tabs
body:
It is hard for users to know which page of the app they are on when their only clue is an icon. Icons can sometimes be ambiguous, and trying to remember their meaning increases cognitive load. We already display page text labels on desktop views, but on small mobile devices the labels disappear (and the vast majority of our users access the app via phones).

We should tweak our design so that we can display page tab text labels even on small mobile views, whenever there are 3 or less tabs. This would add text labels for most CHW views, since most CHWs only see 3 tabs. Users with 4 or more tabs accessing via a small mobile device will still have too many tabs to display text labels, so they will continue to see icons only. 

To accomplish this with our current fontawesome nav icons, slightly decrease the size of the icons, move them up a few pixels, and slightly increase the height of the black mobile header bar to 60px. Text, if displayed, is 12px.
![Header with labels](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/61237083-7bbe3100-a6ee-11e9-9092-27d02be835e4.png)


To accomplish this with our new icons, as implemented in #5535, keep the icons at their standard 24 x 24 size, move them up a few pixels, and slightly increase the height of the black mobile header bar to 60px. Text, if displayed, is 12px.
![Header with labels Copy](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/61237086-7fea4e80-a6ee-11e9-8f7b-dc28335ea74e.png)

title: Infodoc maintanence refactor
body:
Moves infodoc code into a shared library, consolidating code.

Moves the maintenance of the `initial_replication_date` and
`latest_replication_date` into API.  This is a more correct representation of
what these dates should be, as they are now actually when the writes happen not
when sentinel notices they happen. 

Apart from being just "more correct", this fixes a few edge cases:
 - if sentinel is down for whatever reason these dates stay accurate
 - if sentinel touches a legacy document created before infodoc dates it doesn't
   incorrectly update its initial_replicaiton_date to now
 - it removes our quick fix where we presume that a document is only new if its
   rev is 1 or undefined, which will not be true if a CHW creates and then edits
   a data_record while offline.

Moving contacts doesn't update the contact who will receive scheduled messages when no patient_id is set.
body:
**Describe the bug**
We introduced the option to move contacts to new parents in medic-conf. When a report is missing the `fields.patient_id` the doc won't update correctly to the new parent. This causes the scheduled messages to be sent to the previous contact who submitted the report originally. This would need to be updated so that it send to the correct contact under the new parent. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. As an offline user. Go offline
2. Create a new female patient with standard config
3. Process a new pregnancy(this report should have no `fields.patient_id` because it is offline and sentinel hasn't given the patient_id)
4. Go online and sync.
5. Move the newly created patient to a new parent. 
6. Review the scheduled messages

**Expected behavior**
The scheduled messages should be updated to the new correct contact so when they are sent it is sent to the correct person. They currently will send to the original reporter. 

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev
- Browser: chrome
- Client platform: linux
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.6.0

**Additional context**
From @dianabarsan 

> When hydrating a single doc (with fetchHydratedDoc) we end up with the fully hydrated patient lineage, including the primary contacts of the parents, but when fetching in bulk (with hydrateDocs) we end up with minified patient primary contacts lineage, which is required to map patient clinic correctly. The bulk hydration is used when scheduled messages are generated

title: Outbound tasks fail if one of the task documents is deleted
body:
If you create a data_record that creates an outbound task, and then you delete the data_record before the task is sent, it crashes the outbound scheduler and no tasks are sent.

This is happening here: https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/sentinel/src/schedule/outbound.js#L33

We don't filter out results that have no docs, which means null array elements are passed to `hydrateDocs`.

We should correctly detect tasks for deleted documents and delete the associated tasks.

Workaround script to do this manually incoming.

title: Lazy load unread count to reduce visible load time
body:
During our bootstrap process, we spend a lot of time building six mapreduce indexes. Two of these are indexes used by `webapp/src/js/services/unread-records.js`: 

* `medic-client/data_records_by_type` is used to count the total number of reports and the number of messages
* `medic-user/read` is used to count the number of reports read by the logged in user

This count yields a red bubble over the tab. 

![Screenshot from 2019-08-01 00-38-00](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9014751/62274498-d9dc5b00-b3f4-11e9-8d7b-9749e7262090.png)

This decorative data isn't required before first render. Although we don't explicitly wait for it to complete before first render, it likely slows down startup performance by competing for resources in parallel with our critical path (building the other four indexes). 

This seems like an excellent candidate for lazy loading after the bootstrapping is completed.

title: Reports with errors trigger tasks when created/modified but not on reload
body:
**Describe the bug**
If a new report with errors is created or an existing report with errors is modified, that report is passed into the RulesEngine and can trigger a task or a target. When the webapp is reloaded, that report is not passed into the RulesEngine and different tasks/targets will appear.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Clean webapp
1. Update a task in config to log the contact/reports which get passed into partner code. 
1. Create a new report with errors (eg. `await PouchDB('medic-user-ac1').put({ _id: 'test_report', patient_id: 'c8314e6b-8ac6-5a5a-b959-6f58cc015cfe',  type: 'data_record', form: 'test', errors: ['error'] })`)
1. You will see that this report is passed into the partner task/target code.
1. Reload the page
1. You will see that this report is not passed into the partner task/target code.

**Expected behavior**
Tasks and targets should be the same before and after a reload. We apply the same filters to reports on startup as we do when reports are created/modified.

**Performance Impacts**
In `RulesEngine.js` we have this line: [Search('reports', { valid: true }, options),](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/rules-engine.js#L226) which filters the reports to only valid reports.  This filter causes the `medic-client/reports_by_validity` index to be built, which can take a long time during bootstrap. If we queried all reports instead of valid reports, this bug would be fixed and application startup times would improve.

title: MoH Nepal erred reports vs. messages
body:
### Context
Currently, SMSes sent by FCHVs are divided into two webapp tabs:

1. Reports
     - Valid reports — accepted
     - **Invalid (erred) reports — a report-specific error message** is sent with an example of the correct syntax for the type of report that the FCHV was attempting to send, as well as other information pertaining to the specific error that was made

2. Messages
     - **All messages — a generic reply message** is sent, indicating that we have received their SMS, but if they were trying to send a report, they should check the format and resend

**“Invalid Report” - further detail**
If an FCHV sends an SMS such as [form code_space_non-existent ID number], or [form code_space_omission or mistake in required syntax] the SMS is categorized as an “invalid report” in the reports tab. The system recognizes which report the FCHV was attempting to send by the [form code_space], and replies with a report-specific error message, including an example of the correct syntax for that type of report, and any other information to help correct the error that was made ("99999 ID has not been registered, please confirm the ID and resend the form")

**“Message” - further detail**
In the case, however, that the FCHV sends an SMS starting with [form code_no space], the system will categorize the report as a “message” in the messages tab. After receiving any type of “message”, the system sends a generic reply, indicating that if the FCHV was attempting to send a report, it was not recognized, and to check the format and try again. This response does not outline correct syntax or point to other specific errors, as it does not recognize which form the FCHV was attempting to send.


### Feature Requirement

As an FCHV, when I make a mistake in my report, I want to be able to know both that it was a mistake, and how I can correct it, so that I can accurately report on my patient as well as improve my own skills using the mHealth tool.

As a Medic teammate, I want to be able to distinguish form codes followed by no space (a report error) from a free-form message that an FCHV sends through the mHealth tool (text communication) so that I can...
- have an accurate count of, and can therefore analyze, error rates
- have an accurate count of, and can therefore analyze, other indicators pertaining to engagement, performance, and timeliness
- easily sort through SMSes intended as messages to understand what FCHVs are communicating via text (rather than through reports)


### Unmet need or opportunity 

Unmet need: in the webapp and analytics, we currently only capture and categorize certain types of SMS errors, as errors. Therefore, we cannot understand the full extent to which FCHVs are making errors in reports versus sending text messages to communicate.
Missed opportunity: to help FCHVs to correct and learn from their minor mistakes.

**Impact of this “pain” for developers, patients, providers, managers, etc.?**
Analytics data is not entirely accurate (an issue for **Medic**, as well as for **managers** and **health coordinators** as they gain access to external dashboards); this could misguide greater programmatic decisions. **FCHVs** may feel confused or be mislead by receiving clear feedback on certain types of errors, but not others; this could lead to future inaccuracies, missed reporting, and/or a feeling of discouragement.


### Proposed solution

**Describe how you would like to solve the “pain” that you identified:**

- Categorize any SMS starting with [form code_no space_number], as an “invalid report” rather than a “message”, generating the correct report-specific error message, thereafter
- Categorize any SMS starting with several characters linked together as a "message", except for the following characters: **जघद, जघ, जस, जश, जष, जसद, जशद, जषद,** as these are potential report attempts for delivery (if an FCHV forgot to put a space between the form code and the delivery type)

OR

- Categorize any SMS starting with [form code_no space_a character or number], as an “invalid report” rather than a “message”, generating the correct report-specific error message thereafter. This potential solution may, however, capture many SMSes intended to be "messages", as "invalid reports"
 
**Examples of the future fix:**
A 25 Sarita (अ 25 सरिता) = valid report
A Sarita 25 (अ सरिता 25) = invalid report, triggers error message
**P25 Sarita (अ25 सरिता) = invalid report, triggers form-specific error message (proposed change)
JSD 35105 3 (जघद 35105 3) = invalid report, triggers form-sepcific error message (proposed change)**
Baby 25 Sarita (बच्चा 25 Sarita) = message
Sarita is having a baby! = message



### Example use case for this feature

All use cases in Nepal MoH deployments


**Provide an example of the solution value in terms of the “pain” it will alleviate using a real-world application:**

**FCHV Rama** is trying to register Sarita’s pregnancy. She makes an error in her form by forgetting to put the space between the form code and Sarita’s age. She receives a report-specific error message in reply, telling her that there was an error, and that if she wants to register a woman’s pregnancy, to please try again using this format: [अ age name]. Rama tries again, successfully registers Sarita’s pregnancy, and learns from her mistake.

**Municipality Health Coordinator Mina** has an accurate view of the FCHV error  and engagement rates of each HF in her municipality, and can therefore make an informed decision about where to prioritize refresher trainings.

**Service Designer Danielle** has access to accurate data about the most frequently erred reports, in order to inform the redesign of form structures and syntax.


### Links to supporting information

[Nepal MoH Basic Messaging Deep-Dive](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ktjIdcjpqeR76qrmtKaEN68J53c6T4VCZRlUR-eXGGE/edit#gid=0) - a look into SMSes received to understand what FCHVs are communicating via message, and how many “messages” are actually erred reports

cc: @ranjuts

title: Server side purge
body:
# Description

Adds serverside pseudo purge which runs on a schedule and executes a configurable "purge" function over all docs that would be replicated. "Purged" docs are added in auxiliary databases - one for every unique user roles group.
During offline user replication (both initial and subsequent), only docs that are not tagged as "purged" are downloaded. On a schedule, on application bootstrap, the webapp will check if new documents were "purged" and delete them from the device.

medic/medic#5443

# Long description

Executes a pseudo server-side purge which:
- runs on a configurable schedule
- computes a list of unique role groups from all existent users, each unique role group purges being saved in a separate database
- compiles groups consisting of: a contact, reports _about_ the contact, messages that the contact has sent or received
- over each doc group and for each role group, runs a configurable purge function which accepts the group + the roles as parameters and is expected to return an array of doc_ids which should be purged
- queries the purge dbs and compare the resulting list of purged ids compared to the existent purged docs and saves the differences (deleting old purges or by adding new)
- a doc is purged for a list of roles if a document with the same id, prefixed with `purge:`, exists in the corresponding purge database (eg. `purge:this_is_my_doc_id`)

When performing an initial replication:
- users will only download changes for docs that are not purged for their role set 
- the list of purged doc ids is cached for 5 minutes (with refreshed ttl)
- after initial replication, webapp calls an api endpoint which will create a "checkpointer" doc in the corresponding purge db that saves the current `update_seq`

When performing any replication:
- users will only download changes od docs that are not purged for their role set

On bootstrap, every 7 days or configurable via `purge: run_every_days` or when user roles change: 
- webapp calls an api endpoint which will query _changes from the corresponding purge db from the seq saved in the checkpointer doc
- the endpoint returns a list of new purged doc ids and the a seq of the purge db
- webapp deletes the docs locally, also marking them as purged
- webapp queries an api endpoint that updates the purge checkpointer doc using the seq received in the previous response

title: Offline users download all their previous feedback docs
body:
**Describe the bug**
When a user is setup on a new device, they download all docs from their meta-db. Previously, the meta-db only contained `read` docs, which are relevant to the user, so the replication is not filtered. However, since https://github.com/medic/medic/commit/a0c57b1908f7b14dbcf008d0f84564d00fb1ff70 , users also store their `feedback` docs in the meta DB, which will also be downloaded when users setup a new device. These docs occupy storage space without being of any use whatsoever. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Login as an offline user and create a feedback doc (you can do this from the hamburger menu -> Report bug). 
2. Refresh the page to trigger meta db sync. 
3. Wipe device data and login with the same user. Wait until all networking is finished. 
4. Check your local meta db and observe that you have downloaded the feedback doc you created before. 

**Environment**
- Instance: any 3.5 + instance
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.5+

title: Updates to reminders
body:
# Description

Updates reminders to:

- Not update leaf (clinic) docs to add a task for every reminder. Instead, create docs with significant
ids for every reminder task. The id pattern for these docs is `reminder:<form>:<reminder_date>:<place_id>`. They also have a new type `reminder`, so no offline users will replicate them. They are visible in the admin message queue and picked up as "pending" messages by the outgoing SMS services. The uniquely deterministically id-ed docs also make it easy to check if a reminder doc already exists for a place for a specific reminder instance.

- Not depend on a specific view (`medic-sms/sent-reminders`) to determine whether a reminder instance has been sent, instead, after every successful reminder instance run creates a log doc stored in `medic-sentinel` (`reminderlog:<form>:<reminder_date>`) that can be checked by compiling the expected id from reminder config. 

- Not depend on having a specific transition (`update_sent_forms`) update leaf (clinic) docs to add a `sent_forms` property storing the last date a form, that has a corresponding `reminder` config, was created by the primary contact of the place. Instead, with a slight update, make use of an underused existent view (`medic/reports_by_form_and_parent`) to get this date value.

title: Fully hydrate patient lineages in LineageModelGenerator and Shared-lib/Lineage
body:
# Description

This is a fix to our lineage code which fixes the two user-facing bugs identified in #5824. 

1. The UI fails to correctly identify the contact which will receive a scheduled message (bug in LineageModelGenerator)
1. Sentinel actually fails to send the message to the correct contact (bug in the lineage shared library hydrateDocs)

These bugs are both due to code paths which hydrate documents incompletely.

### LineageModelGenerator

This service implements three hydration code path for specific document types (`report`, `contact`, and `reportSubjects`). These interfaces reuse some of the code from the lineage shared-lib, but the `report` interface has a different output than the shared-lib's `fetchHydratedDoc`/`hydrateDocs` interfaces (bug). In the long term, it is my opinion we should consolidated to one interface for hydrating documents `hydrate(thing, options)`. This change moves toward that end by removing one of the custom hydration code paths in the LineageModelGenerator.

In this change, I've refactored LineageModelGenerator.report to use shared-lib's fetchHydratedDoc. This has the following affects on that interface:

* The report is now fully hydrated (bug fix).
* The `merge` parameter (ala `LineageModelGenerator.report(id, { merge: false })`) is no longer supported. In our code, it was always true.
* Returns a model without a lineage attribute. I did a reasonable scan through the code paths and believe it to never be used.

### Lineage Shared-Lib 

* Improve separation of concerns by splitting into multiple files (hydration/minification)
* Non-functional ES6ification 
* Add `{ options }` parameter to the `fetchHydratedDoc` interface supporting `throwWhenMissingLineage` (default: false). This allows the change in LineageModelGenerator to maintain the failover behavior.
* Update hydrateDocs to properly hydrate the patient's parents and the patitent's parent's contacts.

### Performance Impacts

I think these numbers are just very noisey.... I'm rerunning these:

The numbers for for offline users:

title: Replace underscore with lodash in replication
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
We're currently doing two calls to `underscore`'s `uniq` function in our replication code:
here: https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/api/src/services/authorization.js#L185
here: https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/api/src/services/authorization.js#L234

This is done because we might end up with duplicates when querying views that will result in multiple changes for a single doc (CouchDB will return a change as many times as it's id exists in the request list). 

Unfortunately, the implementation of `underscore`'s `uniq` (and likely other array functions) has very poor performance and is also resource blocking.
```
const _ = require('underscore');
const uuid = require('uuid');
_.uniq(Array.from({ length: 100000 }).map(() => uuid()));
```
This code snippet takes a whooping 39 seconds to execute on my machine. Granted this is an extreme case, but there have been misconfigured users that have this many docs. It would be nice to not block API sorting their allowed doc ids.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Straight up replacing `underscore` with `lodash` looks like a good solution.
```
const lodash = require('lodash');
const uuid = require('uuid');
lodash.uniq(Array.from({ length: 100000 }).map(() => uuid()));
```
This code snippet takes 0.39 seconds to execute. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively we could write our own array/object functions and put them into a shared lib. 

**To Reproduce**
Create a misconfigured offline user (to have a significant impact, have at least 50 000 docs). Login with that user and start replicating. 
In the same time, logged in as an online user, try to browse the app and observe if it's responsive or not. 

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: 3.7

title: Login page dynamic elements don't work correctly
body:
**Describe the bug**
Because the login page is cached by the service worker, any code that gets run when that page gets rendered only gets run once, at the point that the device first visits the login page. You can see all this code in [`login.get`](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/api/src/controllers/login.js#L186).

This logic includes:
 - White labeling / branding
 - Translations
 - Redirection (though this appears to be additionally broken by other code as well)

It gets more complicated, because somehow regardless after you wipe the service worker to force it to call `login.get` again fresh, the *next* reload defaults the login page back to a vanilla version, e.g. with no redirect url (despite what you passed it) and English (despite what your language is set to).

**Reproduction steps**

(bonus, boot api with a debugger via `node --inspect server` etc and put a break point in `login.get` for extra details)

1. Successfully and completely log in to the application as any English-language user (I used a online user) into an environment with multiple languages
2. Change your user's language to something else (e.g. French)
3. Log out
   - Here you would **expect** the login page's language to be French, but you **observe** it's still English
   - (also note that `login.get` never ran)
4. Unregister the service worker, by (in Chrome) going to dev tools -> Application -> Service workers and clicking 'Unregister' for your URL
5. Refresh the login page
   - (notice now `login.get` runs)
   - Note that the login page is now in French
5. Refresh the login page **again**
   - (once again `login.get` doesn't get run)
   - Note now that the login page is **back to English**  

**Environment**
- Instance: Localhost running master
- Browser: Chromium 76
- Client platform: Linux
- Version: master

title: Run e2e's CouchDB fresh each time via Docker
body:
Uses docker and tmpfs mounting to provide a completely fresh CouchDB instance to
locally run e2e tests.

Travis is not affected.

This stops e2e results from polluting your CouchDB, including your `_users`
database.

CouchDB is left running under 4984 so you can inspect the DB if you wish. It
will get cleaned out on computer restart or on the next e2e call.

Additionally e2e tests will probably run faster locally as they are now
effectively running CouchDB out of a RAM drive.

It requires Docker to be installed in such a way that `docker` is available on
the command line.

title: Store PA risk scores in the patient
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, predictive algorithm risk scores are calculated in the app in both tasks and targets and in the contact summary. This creates duplication of code, is a potential source of technical debt, and leads to unnecessary computation.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A better implementation of risk scoring is to set a minimum refresh window (e.g., 1 day, 1 week, 1 month) and store the risk score and its calculation date in the patient to be accessible by tasks, targets, forms, and contact summary. Scores would then be recalculated only when the age of the risk score is greater than the minimum refresh window.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Risk scores loaded to the contact page from the server side are infeasible in an offline-first context where we cannot guarantee that they will reach the phone in time to be of use.

**Additional context**
Depending on the approach taken in our screening work with PIH, this may be useful for implementation in that project in April 2020.

This is also relevant as we consider expansion and scale-up of our predictive algorithms initiatives through recently launched data science partnerships. These partnerships would be looking to close out in mid-2020, with implementation possibly in late 2020.

title: Format data for sending to DHIS2
body:
https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5661 introduces the ability to calculate data for sending to DHIS2. Prior to sending this data to DHIS2 (or downloading it as a file to be uploaded), we'll need to format it in a way that DHIS2 can process. The DHIS2 documentation related to these formats can be found [here](https://docs.dhis2.org/master/en/developer/html/webapi_data_values.html#).

While there are a number of different formats supported, here is an example payload to help illustrate a few points. 

~~~JSON
{
  "dataSet": "pBOMPrpg1QX",
  "completeDate": "2019-10-03",
  "period": "201909",
  "orgUnit": "DiszpKrYNg8",
  "dataValues": [
    { "dataElement": "f7n9E0hX8qk", "value": 21 },
    { "dataElement": "Ix2HsbDMLea", "value": 17 },
    { "dataElement": "eY5ehpbEsB7", "value": 14 }
  ]
}
~~~

A `dataSet` is essentially a grouping of `dataElements` for the purposes of data entry. In Kenya, the **MoH 515 CHEW Summary** is an example of a `dataSet`, and the core dimensions that describe data in DHIS2 are as follows (*All data values will at a minimum have these 3 dimensions*):

- The **where** : *organisation unit* (ex. Bondo CHU)
- The **what** : *data element* (ex. Total Deliveries)
- The **when** : *period* (ex. September 2019)

Data can also be disaggregated further using `categoryOption` and `categoryOptionCombo`.  The diagram below attempts to illustrate the relationship between all these dimensions.

So for each of the calculations we define in https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5661 , at a minimum we'll need to map to a `dataElement`, and possibly a `categoryOptionCombo` as well.

![DHIS2 Data Set Hierarchy](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/66392678-4b85e600-e9f0-11e9-8d88-db7465b0370d.jpg)

title: Timeout option is not set during replication
body:
**Describe the bug**
During initial replication, the `timeout` option to PouchDB is [set to 10 minutes](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/index.js#L103).  During routine replications, the `timeout` option is [not set](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/db-sync.js#L52) and uses PouchDB's default.

**Expected behavior**
The two replications should have matching timeouts.

**Additional context**
We should make this change in 3.8 along-side the features around writing tasks to disk since that feature is expected to increase the document count which will increase the time spent in _changes requests.

title: Outbound can halt scheduler execution permanently
body:
**Describe the bug**
We have noticed (cc. @senseibara) instances where the outbound push scheduled task appears to freeze, in one case a week before we restarted sentinel. This doesn't kill Sentinel completely, instead somehow the outbound promise chain never resolves (or rejects), which causes the scheduler to not progress, which also means nothing ever gets rescheduled.

No reproduction steps right now, it happened once once and there wasn't any interesting log output. Restarting sentinel pushed it forward (it processed 20 documents and then froze again, restarting it once more processed the last dozen or so).

The only two guesses I have are:
 - There is an instance where we haven't coded the flow right and we're breaking the promise chain (e.g. we manually create a promise because we're mixing in callbacks, and `resolve()` or `reject()` never get called)
 - Some piece of I/O that we're doing doesn't have a default timeout configured and is blocking indefinitely

title: Make sure app versions are always in sync
body:
**Describe the issue**
We display app versions in two places with two different sources
1. The logo tooltip is set using an Angular constant which is set when Grunt builds the app by pulling it out of the package.json.
2. In the About page which pulls it from the deploy_info on the local medic-client ddoc. This only exists for tagged releases and falls back to the package.json version for development builds, alpha releases, etc.

Updating the package.json is a documented step of the release process but it's easy to miss, which leads to [last minute bugs](https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/6048).

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I can see two possible solutions...
1. Add a test or build time check which fails the build when a tag is created that doesn't match the package.json version, but that'll fail late in the process.
2. Set the package.json version to 1.0.0 permanently and show "unknown" for the version for non-tagged releases. This cleans up the code a little, removes a step from release management, and means the version will always be correct (unless unknown).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Nagging people constantly...
